Yet, regardless of how or when you observe it, is it not your misfortune if you cannot grasp its true nature and practical application? Is a mere superficial glance at the yam sufficient? Certainly not.

Faith is undeniably a virtue. However, clinging to a static belief, demanding that faith must always manifest in a specific, predetermined manner, is impractical. If one merely adopts the ancestral notion that a single glimpse of the divine is sufficient and equates to absolute realization, what can be achieved? Such a simplistic approach is inadequate. What benefit do we derive from merely tallying the yams in our own possession against those held by others? It is akin to the proverb, "If the father arrives, there will be jaggery." But what if the father fails to arrive? Therefore, you must diligently account for what is presently in your own grasp. You have initiated the process of claiming your rightful inheritance; you must complete that reckoning. What if you refrain from this accounting, assuming the keys remain safely with the grandfather? Everything exists, situated right where it belongs. However, the grandfather has passed away. This is the crucial reality that must be comprehended.

Each of you possesses potential proportionate to your own capacity. In life, the measures of fortune, virtuous deeds, sin, and merit vary significantly among individuals. A mere vision of the Divine is insufficient. Our very approach to invoking the Divine is fundamentally flawed. This exemplifies the faith of a Shudra. Kamsa serves as the paradigm of this Shudra faith; his spiritual evolution halted at that specific juncture. He witnessed it, placed his faith in it, and sought experience, mystical powers, and knowledge entirely through that limited paradigm, never progressing beyond it. Consequently, he failed to comprehend the true significance of the ethereal voice (*Ashariri*). Therefore, an individual who has ascended only to the level of Kamsa is inherently incapable of distinguishing between *Advaita* (non-dualism) and *Dvaita* (dualism). This is the defining characteristic of the Shudra varna. All the preceptors (*Acharyas*) who have emerged thus far remain stagnant at this level. This realization dawns only upon reaching the ultimate state. One might confess, "This is not it, Lord; I was gravely mistaken. I harbored the conviction that nothing exists apart from You." However, upon arriving there, one discovers a multitude of entities, some equal and many superior to oneself. It is these forces that govern the cosmos. This is the precise predicament of all such preceptors.

If you fail to grasp this profound truth and merely attempt to attain fulfillment by marveling at, singing about, and blindly acting upon the ancient accounts narrated by others, your fundamental misconceptions will never be eradicated. One must advance beyond the stagnation point of Kamsa and these preceptors, progressing to a state where one can comprehensively decipher and resolve the manifested course of karma.

How many billions of people inhabit this world? Within this solar system, there are six billion. If one were to attempt progression by narrating the individual experiences of every single person, advancement would be utterly impossible. The distinction between *Dvaita* and *Advaita* was formulated as a simplified heuristic to address this complexity. The manifestations of *Dvaita* are fundamentally uncountable; they perpetually shift and evade precise categorization.

Yogis adopt various practices—such as *Hamsa Yoga*, *Hatha Yoga*, and *Chandrika Yoga*—to loosen the physical bonds of their limbs and clear somatic blockages like phlegm. Does this physiological mastery imply the attainment of perfect spiritual wisdom? In contemporary times, any celebrated yogi is readily proclaimed a *Hamsa Yogi*. However, allowing this metaphorical swan (*Hamsa*) to flutter about indiscriminately without true realization will not yield the desired ultimate objective.
Guruvani
March 2003

I have frequently explained the essence of *Guru Pooja* to you, tailored to the context of various occasions. Yet, what is your actual comprehension of *Guru Pooja*? Merely worshipping the Guru—nothing beyond that. While *Guru Pooja* is conducted in numerous locations, it is not a universally practiced ritual even across India. In North India, the term *Guru Pooja* is widely used. However, they too have failed to grasp its profound magnitude beyond the superficial act of revering the Guru. At Santhigiri, *Guru Pooja* is performed with a distinct and deeper significance. Nevertheless, even long-standing members of this community remain largely ignorant of its true dimensions. There are fundamental reasons preventing you from achieving that requisite level of familiarity and understanding.

Among the *Brahmin*, *Kshatriya*, *Vaishya*, and *Shudra* categories, the first three possess a rudimentary capacity to understand when instructed. However, when it comes to the *Shudra* varna, there is an absolute void of such spiritual awareness. What precisely is a *Shudra*? It is not the designation of a caste, but rather a *varna* (an occupational and spiritual classification). Historically, they were disenfranchised from undertaking authoritative spiritual practices. It is widely propagated that even the *Manu Smriti* mandates this restriction. Yet, this represents a gross misinterpretation of Manu's injunctions. The error lies in the arbitrary systems imposed by later individuals claiming to interpret Manu. Given this entrenched situation, through what means, in what manner, and at what juncture are we supposed to exert our agency and achieve realization?

The unique essence of *Guru Pooja* at Santhigiri lies in the intimate bond between the Guru and the disciple. The *Shudra* varna is only capable of perceiving this Guru-disciple relationship as a transactional ritual of offering oblations and displaying superficial respect. Presenting offerings and exhibiting reverence does not constitute true *Guru Pooja*. Despite repeatedly hearing, witnessing, and intellectually engaging with this concept in various forms, you fail to internalize it. Even when kept in close proximity and guided through the practices, comprehension remains elusive. The individual lacks even fundamental self-awareness. This exemplifies the profound ignorance inherent in the *Shudra* varna. However, this cannot be entirely attributed as their fault, for a historical decree was imposed explicitly barring them from active participation. This is the root cause. While the *Vaishya* possessed the liberty to engage in labor and commerce, they too were marginalized from the core procedures of worship. Regarding the purity of lineage (*Gotra Shuddhi*), the strictures of the Vedic religion served as their absolute authority as well, consequently depriving them of true lineage purity. Both of these varnas remain utterly ignorant of the protocols required to attain *Gotra Shuddhi* or the profound nuances of true worship. The *Shudra* is omnipresent as a facilitator and servant in all spheres, yet remains entirely excluded from the esoteric core of these matters. Thus, through generations, this varna suffered a catastrophic loss of *Dharma*. *Kali Yuga* is, in fact, the era uniquely designed for reclaiming this monumental loss. Contrastingly, we have been indoctrinated to believe that *Kali* signifies absolute destruction. If *Kali* is merely annihilation, what purpose does human birth serve in this epoch? Alternatively, should we postpone our existence until *Kali* concludes? The mechanics of *Dharma* operate on an entirely different paradigm.

In the chronological progression of the *Yuga Dharma*, *Kali Yuga* constitutes the fourth quarter. Whosoever takes birth during this epoch—whether a *Brahmin*, *Kshatriya*, *Vaishya*, *Shudra*, or even a *Chandala*—possesses an undeniable, fundamental right to liberation (*Mukti*). *Kali Dharma* is the precise mechanism that unequivocally guarantees this right. Recent history provides ample empirical evidence to solidify this assertion. The most paramount example is the very incarnation of Lord Sri Krishna. Krishna manifested within the *Shudra* lineage. Yet, despite being born in a *Shudra* clan and ascending to royal authority, Kamsa remained fundamentally incapable of comprehending this divine reality. Nevertheless, from an alternative perspective, it is inaccurate to assert that Kamsa lacked awareness. On the contrary, Kamsa was a believer of unwavering conviction. He possessed substantial intellect, a capacity for devotion, and profound dedication. He was endowed with the mystical capability for direct esoteric vision. Therefore, he should not be misconstrued as an ignorant fool. What, then, constituted his fatal flaw? He critically lacked the supreme spiritual knowledge (*Atma Vidya*) required both to abide by *Dharma* and to implement it. Furthermore, he was entirely oblivious to the rigorous path necessary to attain that transcendental *Atma Vidya*.

People often ask if the manifestation of the Lord is not enough. What is the purpose of this manifestation? Is this manifestation meant for blessing and destruction? That is how the scrutiny of Dharma is performed at the end of every epoch. But this is not *Atmavidya* (Self-knowledge). We cannot do anything to remove the mistake we have made through this concept of blessing and destruction. Moreover, the ignorance regarding blessing and destruction continues to persist. How can this be changed?

Today, we cannot achieve anything by dividing ourselves along the lines of caste and religion and dancing wildly. There is no point in fighting either. Is there a need to fight for God? If you, living in your own land, have different Gods, shouldn't you just move away from that land? It is because you worship God as separate entities that you have suffered the misfortune of fighting among yourselves. It is because of this blindness of caste and religion that you could not be saved even though Sri Krishna came.

Even though an advance notice was given that the birth of Sri Krishna would happen in a certain way, what all was done by failing to respect it? He was chased to all parts of India without being allowed to stay in one place. Instead of understanding this series of events in that manner, what do you have in your hands other than the ruined traditional actions, celebrating the story of the Pandavas and the tale of whether the wax palace was burnt down or not, treating it all as a mere play and matter of importance? And then, you have been misled into believing that this is *Atmavidya*. This notion is the biggest among the blunders that have occurred to this day.

There is a trick behind the Shudra conception of Sri Krishna. This trick is a puzzle thrown in front of the Shudra. What is it? The imagination of him being the husband of sixteen thousand and eight women. By leading you into a completely unnecessary action, nurturing you in that tendency, and making males and females dance up to the Balagokulam, they have completed the process and turned you into the remnants of ignorance. What can be done about the vileness that has cultivated this ignorance through the worship of God? Is it from this vileness that one should strive to reclaim *Atmavidya*? *Atmavidya* does not have such a nature. And one should never assume that it does. Furthermore, no one should think that they can be saved by climbing to the pinnacle of Vedanta, claiming that this does not exist. Who can be improved by babbling about things that are of no use to the living? It is simply wasting time by blabbering without any significance. This will only serve to push one into actions where the aspect of spiritual merit cannot be illuminated within the Dharma of living as men and women. If the degradation of Dharma that has occurred within just five thousand years is this much, just think how immense the magnitude of the degradation that has come over very long periods would be.

Now let us look at how it has been played out in another way. Who is to be improved by demonstrating the worship method shown in the character of Sri Rama and by ritually enacting the coronation (*Pattabhishekam*) of Sri Rama's time? The coronation of Sri Rama is a trajectory of action that pushes one into destructive deeds performed merely as a play. Because we, our ancestors, and each one of us have done so, living without any certainty about the epochs, we are unable to determine the Dharmas of the times. That is why it had to be said that Kali is destruction. And yet, in another place, they also say that Kali is the best among the epochs. Why are both these things being said in the same breath - is it for you or for the world? Is it the job of these speakers to impose this ignorance? We neither know this by ourselves nor can we ask and find out.

How long will we live on this earth? Can we live until the end of the Kali Yuga? But the actions required to live in the Kali Yuga have not been taught to us. Nor has it been told how to overcome the Kali Yuga through our lives.

The Satya Yuga has passed away truthfully itself. We saw what happened in the Treta Yuga and the Dvapara Yuga. What was spoken to Kamsa as an unembodied voice (oracle) is itself the proof. What was said? - You should not look up. Work for whatever you see in front of you. But Kamsa did not understand that. Because he happened to belong to the Shudra class. Except for those belonging to the Brahmana and Kshatriya classes who became kings in recent times, no one understood it. In Kerala, the majority of kings have come from the Shudra class. What buffoonery was shown to make them Kshatriyas! *Hiranyagarbham*! - Making a golden cow and making them pass through its belly without bending. And then, if a sacred thread is given, it is all settled! And before that, a *Murajapam* too. If asked why this is done, no one knows. If one becomes a king like this, who will get what benefit? Will the rulers or the ruled get any benefit? What is the knowledge gained along with the kingdom? Ages have passed by, caught in this kind of ignorance. Authority was converted into money, power, and wealth, and rejoicing upon it, growing arrogant, it transformed into the absolute form of absurdity. Who can change this situation, and how? You, who move forward considering caste, religion, and class as virtues, will become the owners of actions that degrade you to the level of the god of death (*Kala*). This will never set you right. If the Brahmana is playing by creating Mantras, and through Mantras Tantras, and through Tantras Yantras, and is doing only that action today, how will he live? Today, he is even ready to go to Persia. For what, to perform *Rakta Pushpanjali* (floral offering with blood)? It is easy to take the blood of all those slaughtered there and perform the *Pushpanjali*, isn't it?

Having cultivated vile tendencies in this manner, we have completely become warriors of destructive actions. We dance and play in the world as long as we have health. After that, we become unwanted by anyone. Do you think that by listening to the story of Ajamila and calling out to God at the very end, God will jump and arrive? Or do you think God will come if you get goosebumps listening to the story of bursting out of a pillar to scoop out and eat blood and intestines? God does not come like that at all. The life of one who has fallen into this kind of blindness and jumped around will simply evaporate after death, and the body will merely sprout grass.

The traditional wealth of each of us consists of the ruined actions that have completely faded away behind the demons who died singing and playing, standing in the Dharma that spreads blindness behind the ignorance ruined by stories. It is not being said that nothing in the world exists. It certainly does exist. But what is it that we should attain? We should acquire the knowledge of whatever good can be done for the respective times through our birth and death. We must give respect to whichever era we are born into—an era that comes into being, exists, and perishes. And having lived here for ten or a hundred years, we must take with us the Karma that reaches us. However, it is an ignorance devoid of any such thought that we are imparting through worship. What is that?

One group slaughters and sheds blood. Another group prepares and offers it as a sacrament. Along with that, wine and other things. We have understood this as the worship of God. The karmic flaw of this degraded method of worship is present in all religious doctrines. Do we need liberation from this or not?

We have done whatever anyone has said. But we have not achieved what needs to be achieved through human life. We acquired everything that should not be acquired. Whatever caste or religion we belong to, the situation is the same. If it is said that something good has sprouted in any one religion or caste, it is contrary to the truth. A great person or a visionary at the beginning who created a religious doctrine might have told us the truth. But after that, if one gets caught up in actions based on the advice of an ignorant person, that action will remain. Yet, they will also teach and claim that there is no Karma.

It is true, one who is free from Karma is the master of everything in this world. But how does Karma cease? We do not know about that. Having mistakenly assumed that there is no Karma, we are bankrupt regarding the consciousness of where Karma ceases. There is no such scenario where Karma ceases when the body ceases to exist. If there is, it must be achieved while being alive. We have evidence before us of many who have shown this while alive.

What is the nature of our familiarity today? We divide ourselves by caste, religion, and class, engage in quarrels and brawls, and then proceed to worship God. Does God reside within caste and religion? You are incapable of even contemplating this. Apart from indulging in activities like playing Balagokulam, enacting Sree Rama Pattabhishekam, performing Gurusi, Kuthiyottam, Theyyam, and offering blood to Kali—and whatever other reprehensible practices exist—what do you genuinely understand about worshipping God? Wherever a vacant field is found, you assemble these grotesque effigies, conduct spectacles and ceremonial baths (*Aaraattu*), and invoke God!

You also say that the Guru is Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, and the Supreme Brahman. How does a Guru attain such glory? If you merely invoke the Guru in principle like this, will the Guru actually manifest? The Guru is not someone who comes to bestow blessings or inflict punishments upon you. You do not require such blessings or punishments. While you exist in the awareness of the states of wakefulness (*Jagrat*), dream (*Swapna*), and deep sleep (*Sushupti*), this realization must dawn upon you. That conviction must remain until karma is entirely severed from the soul. You yourselves must be able to witness how that karma is severed.

You possess absolutely no knowledge regarding this path. All that you have heard are mere fragments of Vedanta. Or else, a Gayatri Mantra that combines everything. Do you believe that by going beyond that and repeatedly chanting the Brahmasutra, you will become a Vedantin? What have you assumed? Merely reciting the names of a pile of timber will not make a house. For it to become a house, the timber must be assembled according to its proper width and design.

That is not what is being said. Rather, it is demonstrating right before you what Dharma is in the karma that connects the life and the soul. For that, the spiritual merit (*Sukrita*) pertaining to the soul is required. If you divide yourselves by caste, religion, or class, you will not be able to imbibe this. The period during which a Guru lives and the place where the Guru resides—that is the most sacred and filled with merit. It is often said that a place without a sage (*Sadhu*) is a ruined place.

How have we understood the term 'Sadhu'? You have understood that 'Sadhus' mean poor people. That is not so. A Sadhu is a Sanyasin (ascetic). But a Sanyasin is not a wandering beggar. We boast about all sorts of wandering ascetics by pointing at them! If you are taught such corrupted notions, what will you do? Every religion teaches the exact same thing regarding a Sanyasin. This is another manifestation of the calamity that has befallen the world.

What is the karma of Kali (the present age)? It is a karma that must be handled as meticulously as a gooseberry held in the palm of one's hand. The Guru demonstrates to you that very karma through the transitional states of gross (*Sthula*), subtle (*Sukshma*), effect (*Karya*), and cause (*Karana*). The Guru then reveals how your life interacts with the Guru, or the Guru lineage (*Guru Parampara*), what the position of that lineage is, and its significance within the worldly karma that has existed to this day. Otherwise, if anyone convinces you that karma does not exist, that what is called karma is an illusion, and that karma does not apply to a Yogi, a Jnani (wise one), a Karmi (man of action), or a Bhakta (devotee), then that is entirely a misguided doctrine. To convincingly impart this in all its glory, there must be a competent Guru, and a Guru lineage qualified to function at all times for that Guru. For this, there must always be a Guru who is as enlightened as the primordial Guru (*Adi Guru*) of that lineage. The unique distinction attained by Santhigiri in this regard is divinely ordained by Brahman.
Guruvani
April 2003

There is a karma that we have been performing up to this very moment today. That karma possesses a truth and a purity. We must act with the awareness of this. One should not simply believe whatever someone else says. The knowledge and experience required for us to act are bestowed upon us by God. We should not squander what God grants us. Whatever God bestows will undoubtedly be beneficial to all of us.

No matter who we are, we are individuals who have lived based on a certain faith. This applies to people of any caste or religion. When faith went astray somehow, with the repetition of religious dogmas, and through further misinterpretations and retellings, it became impossible to even comprehend the practical application (karma) of the doctrine. Each one of us is the remnant of such outdated theories of karma. No one can rectify it instantly. Depending on the hardships endured by some individuals and their willingness to suffer, the magnitude of the error can be reduced. When a suitable opportunity arises, it will diminish rapidly. Then, the impact of that error will be akin to a mere cut on the finger where a major calamity was destined to occur.

Our subject is how this archaic karmic trajectory can be resolved. If anyone claims that this karmic path—which we and our ancestors have spoken of, practiced, performed, and caused others to perform until today—does not exist, it will not simply disappear. To assert that it will vanish just like that is sheer foolishness. No matter what we do to reinforce it, it will not be eradicated. However, concerning us, there is a divine grace. God Himself has revealed a solution to that stale karma which we have been performing knowingly or unknowingly up to this point. Both men and women in the household must strive equally to realize that solution.

Once the educated and the uneducated, the foolish and the intelligent, the capable and the incapable—all realize that the greatness of God is one and the same, they must not succumb to arrogance thereafter. Alternatively, if an intelligent person becomes arrogant, one can only let him proceed on that path. Being arrogant about one's education and wealth will yield no benefit whatsoever.

Each one of us is the remnant of the ignorance that proclaims, 'God is confined to my caste; God is confined to my religion.' That means we are standing on the wrong side of knowledge. It is a fallacy to assume that some great soul has taken away all my mistakes and the resulting deficiencies, and that I merely need to sit idle now. These mistakes are not something that any great soul can simply wash away.

As far as we are concerned, we must first attain the knowledge to experience the karmic flaws—or the karmic merits—that have originated through our birth. Experience it with awareness. Let sorrow come if it must; nevertheless, I must exhaust it—this should be our objective. Saying, 'Oh, I went there too, it's all the same,' is not true knowledge. If you act upon such a misconception, unimaginable destruction will befall you. No matter how much pain or hardship we endure, we must handle and resolve this.

How are we to know what our ancestors have done? Demanding that wealth and nobility should accrue equally to everyone is something that is not going to happen anywhere in the world. One group will claim that they are working hard and suffering. What work, whose work, and for what purpose? What if one works for the welfare of the people? Or rather, what exactly is the welfare of the people? Let each person contemplate this. The house of the one who struggles for the welfare of the people will be ruined, that is all. Some will say they have suffered greatly and have not been able to know what love is. Therefore, these matters cannot be reconciled merely through such statements.

We will only receive what we are destined to get through the karma we painstakingly perform with love, humility, and respect. If one decides to act impulsively, uttering trivial things without love and guidance, it will merely be a rash leap. Nothing will be gained from it. Things will only unfold according to the dynamic course of the soul. If we possess everything but are in a state where we cannot even swallow a drop of water, is that not the misfortune of the soul? Others hold many things that could be done for us. Yet, no one does anything. What can be done? Just because others give us something for a day or ten days, will it suffice for us? Do our children not need to grow up as well? What we must understand is that none of this constitutes the karma of a sense of justice. One can fabricate and say many things about the sense of justice. One can even decree destiny. But that is not the destiny of his soul, is it? Regarding this destiny, men and women are entirely equal. If anyone claims otherwise, it is a guidance that pushes one completely toward a misguided path.

We observe diverse types of politicians and religious ideologues. Do their assertions reflect the true trajectory of the world's karma? Must anyone even articulate the nature of the world? The fault lies neither with those who have made such pronouncements nor with those who reiterate what they have heard. Nothing can be accomplished by making impulsive statements without comprehending the underlying sorrows, knowledge, and experience, as well as their profound depth, spanning the past and the future. Indeed, nothing has ever been achieved in this manner. When such overwhelming evidence stands before us, why do we engage in unwarranted speech and actions?

Like you, I am someone who has suffered a great deal. However, I do not dwell upon those hardships. Could I survive if I were to think like that? It is true that I have suffered. That is its inherent nature. God bestowed a certain dignity upon that suffering. If God provides for us, we must be willing to share it with others. That is true sacrifice. For that, wealth, capability, and resources will all be required.

What is the root cause of our suffering? It is the unbearable burden of our lineage. What constitutes that burden? It is the lack of dharma, fortune, and spiritual merit in our lives. Can one simply go somewhere and discard it in a single day? You should not tell anyone such things. What is being said is incorrect. These are merely deceitful tricks of religious dogmas, pseudo-spiritual justifications, and supposed miracles designed to manipulate people. No one should ever believe in any of this. As far as we are concerned, we possess God's grace. This is the absolute truth. However, one must experience the pain to earn God's grace. We may possess absolutely no knowledge regarding such matters. When we complete our deeds of good and evil, we repeatedly perform rituals according to the doctrines of our respective religions. Consequently, we dance to the tunes of others' logic. What does it matter to you how others dance? That is not what I am stating. No one should assume that they can achieve salvation through contrary actions. Should we presume that it is the father's fault, the mother's fault, the society's fault, or the nation's fault? Everyone bears some blame. The land of our birth lacks fortune. What is the reason for our existence in such circumstances? Is it not sufficient to realize that we are even more unfortunate than that?

Indeed, we are worse than everything else. Our ancestors were those who brought about destruction by mistakenly perceiving loveless actions as love, heavily veiled by an inability to ever comprehend the true trajectories of life. When God grants us an opportunity to transcend this, you—whether as father, mother, husband, or wife—must never behave in a manner that forsakes it. Only then can you attain salvation. Once you abandon it, you will be left with absolutely nothing.

Everything we presently do is divinely ordained action (karma). If we abandon all these and walk away, neither our dharma nor our karma will reach completion. You can eradicate this only if you foster an unwavering resolve, love, and respect to consciously eliminate your sufferings along with the sins and merits accumulated through the ignorance of your ancestors. Otherwise, you will never be able to discard it. Eventually, you will abandon your faith as well. This has been my experience.

Let our ancestral doctrines be either right or wrong. We need not attempt to attain salvation by debating their validity. We have been born. Now, what can we do regarding all this? We can contemplate a time when God has bestowed some grace upon us as an opportunity for this purpose. The trajectory of karma—which enables us to mutually understand, communicate, act, and inspire action—must be a love that aligns with dharma. It must never be a love that depletes our spiritual merit. Destruction will ensue in such cases. You must act with unwavering detachment in this matter. If God provides us the opportunity to methodically execute and facilitate this, we must accomplish it. One must fiercely hold onto that determination—that love and respect. If love, humility, and respect are lost, all that is good will subsequently follow suit and perish. A majority of our ancestors were those who strayed in this manner. We must not be provoked by observing them. You must never believe that someone will grant us anything if they perform purported miracles or display the complete manifestation of mystic powers. It will merely result in the eradication of our love.

Having understood these principles to some extent, you must strive relentlessly. Strive earnestly without squandering time. How many individuals do we see before us who have thus wasted their time and opportunities? Some, overwhelmed by an unbearable excess of supposed love, will exhibit many dramatic behaviors. However, after a while, all their love vanishes! I can only say that a thief has stolen it. I cannot draw you closer by narrating other tales. You may grasp as much as your knowledge and love permit.

Regarding knowledge, I do not intend to thrust profound wisdom upon you. Your knowledge, experience, and maturity are limited. Consequently, you are unaware of the nature of the sins and merits of your ancestors. Let that be whatever it may. I have been born, and I have grown up. Various things have occurred, either in this lifetime or in previous ones. I must attain liberation from all of this. This should be our prevailing thought. Otherwise, there is no point in becoming agitated upon hearing someone else's assertions.

Many have fallen because they failed to act with this realization. Therefore, I am stating this directly to you. We can collectively accomplish whatever can be uplifted through our intrinsic love, respect, and humility. You will experience various afflictions such as disease, sorrow, hardship, and poverty. These are indeed universal among human beings. Certain ailments remain uncured despite treatment. Sometimes, treating one illness leads to another. Yet others are incurable diseases. Although we may cite numerous reasons for all these, the fundamental truth is the lack of spiritual merit in our lives. What can be done to remedy this deficit of spiritual merit? This is an profoundly elusive matter. It remains incomprehensible even to devout believers and those who present themselves as great visionaries. Furthermore, it is immensely difficult to find an individual who can provide a resolution for this.

This issue remains consistent across Hindus, Christians, Buddhists, and Jains alike. We tend to celebrate the traditions we have been practicing for a while. When such a conceptual framework is imparted, this karma transforms into something akin to a disease and a hardship. This afflicts many individuals. Yet, no one articulates the root cause behind its occurrence.

The practice of the majority is to place faith in whichever deity their ancestors worshipped and to occasionally visit and offer prayers. However, one must not assume that this constitutes true devotion to God. We can practice devotion to God in all possible ways. The prevailing concept is that God exists in everything. That is not the case. This conceptual nature has emerged due to numerous errors committed because we failed to comprehend the concept of God by acting in accordance with each respective era.

Numerous individuals who lived in grandeur, and precisely those who lived performing numerous good deeds, have become entangled in such concepts. Would it not raise doubts if one were to state that the cause for all this is a lack of spiritual merit in their lives? Would wealth and capabilities accrue to those entirely devoid of any spiritual merit? However, we must study and ascertain how to utilize that merit, in what form of action that merit remains eternally sustained, and what that merit should be transformed into through our lives. We have been conditioned to believe that upon acquiring a little wealth or capability, one should live grandly, look down upon others, and elevate oneself at their expense. What spiritual merit exists in the lives of us who harbor such mentalities? We possess the cumulative prior experience of having lived in this manner for millions of lifetimes. How can this be transformed?

We live, grow, and die. What is the benefit to our soul (jeevan)? We scrub, bathe, and carry around a stinking body. What will we do if there is no life in this body? What if the soul becomes like a rotten tree? How can this be resolved—no one comes forward to explain all this. Where do we go when we suffer the most? To an astrologer, a sorcerer, some temple, or some swamis. No one should assume that we will attain the aforementioned merit (punyam) from these places. There is nothing special about such a belief. What is the deficiency in our soul? This is the goal: how to remove that deficiency? We do not know this at all.

What we have heard of is the system of the Trinity, or the system of prophets, or the path of the Guru—whatever it may be, shouldn't one follow the path where the word of God is received? If we follow these paths, what will we be able to know about our ancestors after four thousand or five thousand years? If we proceed according to the calculation of epochs (Yugas), billions of matters are involved in it. Can we proceed only after knowing all this? None of these traditions have ever taught us about the Yuga Dharma. This is the reason for the deficiency in all people. We cannot immediately live according to the Yuga Dharma either. But this is the time destined for that.

Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, and Shudra—Varna Dharma is defined by these four. It has not been stated for whom and in which epochs (Yugas) this Varna Dharma applies. Since it is taught that the Dharma of Kali Yuga is bad, most people assume that no Dharma needs to be followed in the Kali Yuga. But that is not the case.

To say that 'Kali is in the Shudra' implies that the Shudra has absolute authority. That is, even a Shudra has the right to Brahma Jnana (knowledge of the ultimate reality). Only a Shudra in the Kali Yuga can attain Brahma Jnana. We must firmly believe that through the Dharma of Kali Yuga, a Shudra can acquire the right to Brahma Jnana. Otherwise, no matter what politics, caste, or religion we speak of, our sorrows will not disappear. The deficiency stemming from the rituals and worship practiced by our ancestors will not vanish, regardless of the realm they exist in. Every household leads a life that has grown stale in that deficiency.

There are many people living in forests and on seashores, worshiping minor gods for minor castes. They have no knowledge of what God is. When they do things based on what they hear and see, everything goes awry. Later, they die and end up somewhere.

There is a sky around this earth. Beyond the layer of the earth, there are three outer spheres—the Earth, the Moon, and the Sun. Between these, certain spheres travel at distances beyond the reach of our eyes. They are called Navajyothis. Otherwise, they are referred to as the sky (Aakasham) or the earth (Bhoomika). There is a calculation like that. Can we function only after knowing all these calculations? These things exist whether we know them or not. We may not be able to comprehend all this within a single lifetime.

Let me tell you some things you can do. When our minds go down while we are doing something, it is due to a deficiency in our soul. Getting a disease while growing up and engaging in various activities is also due to a lack of merit (punyam) in the soul. We are unable to accumulate merit for the soul. This is the collective shortcoming of humankind. An astrologer will look and tell you to do this or that. Doing those things will not yield any results.

Our ancestors who lived here have become gods, goddesses, sages, ascetics, or enlightened beings. Where do they stand after death? Coming as their descendants and dying again, billions of souls thus end up in domains devoid of merit. Children born in those domains become diseased, fail to get what they need for growth when they reach that stage, and lack the ability to accomplish things—this is generally called family curse (kudumbadosham). This is not just a family curse, but a deficiency of the soul. This must be corrected through life itself. Not by rejecting one's husband, wife, or children, but by adequately caring for them. One should not do anything by abandoning their children, father, or mother. We should be able to achieve all this through a life lived together. A fundamental ritual (karmam) that enables this is performed at Santhigiri. That is the Guru Pooja at Santhigiri.
Guruvani
May 2003

I have not failed to see what the Acharyas have acquired and given to the world. However, some of them have introduced practices such as telling miraculous tales at the time of leaving their bodies, attaining dissolution by jumping into a river to discard the body, and the practice of wrapping the body tightly in a thousand cubits of cloth and immersing it in the river Ganga. Among another class of ascetics, there is the practice of sacrificing themselves by jumping into a gorge. Thus, our tradition has operated with many deceptive miracles hidden within rituals. You must think about what can be done to resolve the insignificance that has flowed away and perished in this lack of meaning.

I am narrating my experience. It took many years to identify the aforementioned practices for what they are. Despite a state of helplessness, wondering what I was seeing, what was being said, and where all this would lead, I did not stop my quest. At one point, it was even said that I was beaten and driven out of Varkala. There was also a group who claimed that I left with two young women and was never seen again. Thus, there was a time when such talks amused me. I left Varkala in accordance with an intimation I received, which instructed me not to remain in a place where two people could see me. From there, I went to a house in Manamboor. The people of that house would frequently come and invite me. Two acquaintances also accompanied me. I moved because I received an ethereal voice (ashareeri) warning me that staying there would be dangerous. Those who came with me are the ones who dropped me at Manamboor. While there, someone came with a car to pick me up. I went to Paravoor with him. Upon reaching there, I witnessed the celebrations and affairs of an annual death anniversary ritual (aandushraddham). An evil spirit arrived there. After observing its activities, I returned to Manamboor the next day. When I returned, I was met with quite a reception. This house was situated at the entrance of a fish market. The shops and other properties there belonged to the owners of this house. The people in those shops were waiting with weapons like sticks and wooden clubs. The homeowner, perhaps sensing something at that moment, told me, 'Swami, do not stay here now. You should leave immediately. I will explain things later.' He brought me a dhoti (mundu) and gave it to me. And I left. Meanwhile, they were standing there raising their sticks and clubs, shouting loudly. By God's grace, nothing happened there. I had no idea why all these preparations were made. Without knowing anything, I departed. Only later did I understand the matter.

Because the mother in that house was cured of her illness and the daughter was saved from danger, they used to visit me often. I had written a letter to her, 'Child, you are living in a respectable household. Do not forget that. Whatever the relationship between you two may be, I will talk and resolve it.' Seeing this, the mother and father felt that I had started to lead their child astray. I had sent this letter four years before I went to that house. It was a letter sent after performing a ritual for them. It was this letter that they finally received four years later when I arrived there. That is when they developed this 'affection' for me and felt like 'handling me properly,' as mentioned earlier.

Always, my experience has been like this. Wherever I have gone, I have faced situations where I had to live as an object of humiliation. Even after coming here and spending six or seven years, such an experience occurred. Many patients come here, get treated (solely with sacred ash, holy water, and prayer), and are being cured. Among them, a woman was brought here by her husband for the cure of a mental illness; after being cured, she was taken back home. A few days later, that woman, accompanied by a relative, came to the ashram and expressed a desire to stay for two days. The next day, she was nowhere to be seen. She had not gone anywhere else. She was inside the well. Thus, incidents have emerged in life and performed a destructive dance of devastation. However, all this was not something a human could endure. That I could endure it is solely due to the grace of God. In this manner, in every state—by state, I mean the realm a sanyasi or a brahmachari ought to attain—I am achieving them one by one. How this happens is, according to the calculations of scientists existing in this world, reaching the level of atomic science (whether they call it energy, power, the magnificence of nature, or whatever name they give it)—it is the nature in which life and soul evolve through the covering of the five elements we constantly experience today, the knowledge of the five senses, and the realization of the five sheaths. To integrate all this so perfectly, no other science is of use except the assistance of efforts spanning multiple lifetimes. Because this is a truth within my experience, I am imparting it to you.

An opportunity will arise to understand the experiential truth that is part of a greatness. Otherwise, it cannot be said that these are the adverse effects resulting from me going after any sanyasi, siddha, or deity. We possess a lineage that has been able to perceive up to the system of the Trinity as a visibly manifest dharma. You can firmly believe that it exists. Because, we cannot simply discard the actions performed and caused to be performed by our ancestors. That must come. And it must be grasped right along with it. That is the way to proceed. But when grasping it, you must have knowledge.

What is that knowledge? When a god, goddess, sage, sanyasi, wise man, devotee, and person of action arrive, if there is no lineage of Gurus to impart and make them experience eternal peace, you should not take that path. If you do, you will perish. I have the evidence of thousands of experiences for this. Since that evidence is exclusively mine, I am unbothered by what anyone else might say. I have not embraced any of the traditions I grew up in. Initially, I just walked through them all. Then, I understood the extent of their knowledge. By God's grace, I acquired that knowledge. Taking further years, I comprehended its various aspects. Only after that did I wish to say anything to the people. It has only been a short while since I started speaking.

How should you uphold this lineage? In the course of your karma up to this day, whatever demon, god, goddess, sage, sanyasi, or wise man has entered your guidance, the Guru's greatness will bestow all of it upon you in the animate and inanimate, in form and formlessness, and in light. Or else, it will be made known to you through the Guru's actions. Beyond that, you have received the lineage of a doctrine that is systematically explained. When you merge into this experiential truth, you must be careful about one thing. All you have to suffer, love, and respect is sacrifice. You have not been given wealth and other capabilities merely to rejoice. Let God Himself grant you wealth and capability. Let the fortunate ones enjoy it. Or let the fortunate lineage of descendants enjoy it. Do not let wealth and capability be destroyed through ignorance.

If you hold on to a Guru, that Guru must be able to explain everything from demons to the realm of vampires, and beyond that, what the nature of the Trinity is, in which heaven they exist, and which sphere is their abode. Otherwise, you will fall into a trap, caught in the tumult of magical powers and thousands of tantric practices, and in the actions and inactions of royal servants. Living as subjects of all this, you do not realize that you are being pushed into the deep abyss of karma, capturing a poor section of people possessing some knowledge and making them fight each other. This is my knowledge, proven through experience. You who believe here possess that proof. Whatever demon, god, or goddess appears before you, if told to leave, they will leave. Or, if you say 'you will be burnt to ashes' two or three times, it will be reduced to ashes. That is the power of your Guru. In the name of the Guru, it will be consumed by fire. With that caution, you will be able to grasp this. Then, by earning merit through the karma of this path of dharma, a state of complete prosperity that you must collectively attain is encapsulated before you. You must perceive it broadly and pass it on to the children who have reached the stage of karma. That should be the supreme goal of life.

We know thousands of sacrificial rituals. Thinking that one can attain completion by holding onto the karmic flaws of the Ashwamedha Yaga is ignorance and a path to destruction. It is a path that sows destruction and reaps destruction. When adopting the path of a Guru, one must believe in it completely. You should not hold onto it without substance and take it into your mind. You must be able to change from that method, no matter the hardship. Sitting and chanting mantras, observing a satyagraha in front of a God fortified by caste and religion will not yield any results. Nor has it ever. Those who live adhering to this must also make others adhere to it. This is the path God has given you to emerge forever from the deep pit of ignorance in which your father and mother were trapped. I desire that you should be able to grasp a great doctrine by traveling exclusively along that path. For that, what has been worshipped as Pournami is the most appropriate.
Guruvani
June 2003

What you must note is that when I refer to the ancients, through our interactions and loving associations, we have formed many acquaintances where some, using their limited intellect, trivialize these matters while considering themselves highly intelligent. We cannot even comprehend the nature of this intellect. It is impossible. It is only at the very end that we realize this capability is entirely beyond our grasp. Therefore, we will not be able to assimilate anything. It will result in a situation where we end up losing the very things we have acquired. Once that happens, whatever we do thereafter will be of no avail. Thus, there are certain individuals who have loved and respected me alike. This has happened even among them. The reason it happened to them is that a vast community of our so-called ancestors has died and perished. For these departed souls, we perform certain rituals according to whichever religion or caste we currently believe in. Under the guise of this, followers of each religion perform these in their own ways, yet some find it inadequate. Not just some; the majority are like this. Perhaps one in a hundred might exhibit a change. We remain unaware that such a scenario is enveloping us. The reason for this ignorance is the wealth of experience we have accumulated over a very long period of traversing with our ancestors. It remains embedded within our very life force. The moment we exhibit a vulnerability, that entity infiltrates. Once it enters, it begins to operate. After it becomes active, even if they are one's own children, father, or mother, they will apply that intellect in a manner that suits their own nature. By applying their intellect in such a way, the detrimental effects of this intellect are inflicted upon this life force. I have reminded you of this many times. However, using this intellect, many people perform sorcery and similar petty miracles, and numerous families where such departed spirits stagnate will nurture this in the manner of 'nurturing the wicked like a palm tree.' Having nurtured it, it brings about a completely alienated way of life in them. When this happens, as an example, the ones who fail the most in this regard—not a failure of intellectual prowess, but a failure in life itself—are those from the Vedic religion. Wherever, whoever, and in whatever manner they have worshipped within this Vedic religion, if they acquire numerous virtues through these packaged and structured rituals of worship, all of it will go and accumulate in this deity. This residing deity will then seize it. I do not know if you understand this. You must understand it. After seizing it, all these virtues are drained, and this ancestral spirit is taken and positioned within the karmic sphere of these family members. All of you must pay attention to this. Do not assume this is a trivial matter being discussed. Ultimately, these family members, having supposedly evolved with intellect, capability, and competence, will completely ruin it. I have realized that this has happened to more than half of the families who have approached me. Because the misconception that they are intelligent and knowledgeable sets in, causing them to lean towards that karmic path. Even if they are father and children, or husband and wife, they will unknowingly operate from that intellect. No matter how much they try to suppress and preserve it, they will operate it and it will ultimately recoil upon themselves. It is a path of great destruction. The reason for stating this now is that there are many who have performed Gurupooja.

Therefore, even though this has been told to you many times, and you might understand it to a great extent, a slight misunderstanding will still remain. Through that slight misunderstanding, you will make compromises. When you make such compromises, it transforms entirely into a compromise. I am mentioning a significant issue that has occurred to those standing close to me. By the closest people, I mean the nearest families. However, despite being close, they could not grasp it; moreover, they have altered it in some manner. Nothing can be done. They still will not understand this.

As far as we are concerned, we possess knowledge that has lived on for billions of years. Even if that knowledge is minuscule, akin to the saying 'many drops', it can become a 'great flood'. Such a scenario has arisen. It is among those standing close. Around twenty families from Pothencode itself form this circle. If one considers the sincerity they showed back then, it is immense. They had no knowledge. They did everything that was told. Thus, they completed the tasks. In Varkala, it was difficult to conduct it. Saying that it shouldn't be visible to others, it was brought here, and even here, it was only after two and a half or three years that those matters were finally completed. Those tasks were completed. Then it took five years for it. Later, to make it practical, it took about ten years to put it into practice. It is not possible to gather all this together and present it before you. What is the reason? It is simply that it will not be understood. Did they do it out of any enmity? No. Small words will be slightly misconstrued. But they ended up stalling there. This is to remind you about the families that performed Gurupooja. Hence, even after saying this, you lack the ability to preserve it. This must be done in a specific manner. That is, 'Word is Truth'. You must not overthink its logical aspects, whether less or more. If you think, it is lost. When the intellect is applied, those matters simply wither away. Some operate solely on intellect. That will lead to peril. I am telling this to all of you because I can only speak of it. God is bestowing upon you a karma that needs to be done, caused to be done, and undertaken. That portion given by God, you risk losing due to negligence, or due to a perceived indifference, or under the pretext that intellect is of no use; we are the remnants of countless generations where everyone grew up in such a manner. Some people stood aside, uttered various words, and lost it entirely. Shouldn't I say this? Should I just speak to appease you? Through their actions, everything went downhill. What is this that I am doing? You must think. I am not doing it because I am capable of it. I am acting merely as an instrument. This is the divine will. To impart that divine will to you, it has been brought to you across many epochs over billions of years. However, in all these coming epochs, Kali is the path of salvation. You have been told and made to believe that this Kali Yuga is evil. Let us all ponder this together—is Kali evil? Thus, when the attributes of Kali are described, people are made to act vilely in accordance with this Kali. But Kali is not like that. If one does not behave truthfully, Kali will lead to destruction. You simply do not understand that scenario. How can I make you understand? That has become a great difficulty. In that state, those from Pothencode brought pots, pans, winnows, and all such things, cooked, and at the time of washing them, there wouldn't even be water to drink. There are those among them who washed the vessels and drank that water. Despite undertaking this with such hardship, they could not assimilate it. Because they would trivialize certain words—thinking 'he just says things like that'. With that, it is entirely lost. Observe every household. This is why 'Word is Truth'. Back then, when things didn't work out for two or three people who were observing and speaking here, I had a deep doubt whether I had made a mistake, and that is when this Avadhuta came to Varkala and said: No, 'Word is Truth, Truth is Guru, Guru is God'.

That is to say, the state of the *Trimurti* was attained. It is being imparted from there. That is where the error occurs. Consequently, about ten to fifteen households there fell into this predicament. However, they were unable to discern it. Back then, an instruction was received that two individuals should not be seen together. That is how the arrival here happened. Having arrived here, a massive undertaking spanning six to seven years was executed without anyone's knowledge. Subsequent to its execution, it was gradually initiated. All of these were administered in the form of *Guru Pooja* and various other practices. However, since even the families who performed it, and those who facilitated it, failed to exercise caution in the *karma* of this word, they are all departing one by one. What can I do with you? I can never do anything for you. This is a sorrowful *karma* of mine.
Guruvani
July 2003

We have spoken about the matter of prayer several times. I am reminding you of it once more. It has been a full twenty-five years since we began offering this prayer uninterruptedly. Yet, most of those who have been practicing it since then do not understand it at all. If we ask what it is, our general understanding of prayer among us, or what most have heard and assumed, is that the grace of a deity is sufficient. Then, with offerings and vows, some of us have heard about a one-day *pooja*, a one-day inner *pooja*, or a full-day comprehensive *pooja* (*adakkipooja*)—this is the extent of knowledge we possess. When we speak of a one-day comprehensive *pooja*, looking at the most prominent ones in Kerala today, there are only two or three such temples. One is Thiruvananthapuram, or Vaikom, Ettumanoor; these belong to Travancore. Similarly, moving northwards, there are several temples from Kodungallur up to Kasaragod. That extends almost up to the Parasurama temple. Why is it that we build these temples—especially as grand temples in our Kerala—constructing the *Nalambalam*, followed by the *Pattupura*, *Oottupura*, *Poottupura*, and the *Aanakottil*, filling them with immense embellishments?

We have not been able to question and understand what this is until today. The reason for this inability is that for our ancestors, or consider them to be Kshatriyas—except for imparting the authority of the Vedas to these Kshatriyas here, it is established or ordained that they hold no authority. They are referred to as Rajagurus and the like. Beyond that, if an attempt is made to unite us using the Vaishnava tradition, the Shaiva tradition, and the Shaktheya tradition, we will not unite. Standing in three distinct natures, they became highly embellished and degraded into mere songs, dances, games, clamor, and pageantry, making it impossible for even a child to gain any sense of realization from them. Or whatever is imparted is taken from elsewhere—like Kathakali, which is now carried forward as Kerala's unique identity. Observing this itself, the knowledge of addressing each entity differently is being copied from there. It was transformed into such a state even up to the *Theyyamthullal*, and today the government also highlights it, giving it importance as a folk art. It cannot be said that no one has had the opportunity to think about how much we have grown through this, how much we have absorbed, or how much we have been able to perceive; there have been opportunities. However, despite having these opportunities across various eras, a grave misfortune of time (*kaladosham*) that prevents us from uniting has bound us all together, steering us towards the path of destruction.

We have heard of and known the *karma* called *Sanatana*. But today we are bewildered, unable to distinguish between what is *Sanatana* and what is Hindu (*Haindavam*). The uniqueness of this *Sanatana* is to act in accordance with the knowledge of the times. But we neither know what this time is, nor how to carry it forward. Its nature—whether it is a truth or an untruth practiced by our ancestors, as we have confined our actions following the trajectory of *karma* originating from the *Treta Yuga* after the passing of the *Satya Yuga*—it is a matter of jurisprudence. How did we behave in this; the fourth era is *Kali*. When we speak of *Kali*, what we have assumed is that it belongs to the ignorant or that it is an era of the ignorant. That is completely erroneous; there is a concept they have divided for the four eras, represented as the four Vedas. It is stated that it is Vyasa, known as Krishna Dwaipayana, and so forth. Whatever it may be, this knowledge of ours has left us perplexed. How can we celebrate or proceed hereafter in the *dharma* of this *Kali*?

Stating '*Kali Shudrankal*' (*Kali* resides in the Shudra), *Kali* has operated in a manner that can never be altered. Therefore, when it was proclaimed that *Kali* belongs to the Shudra, many of us felt 'we are great people,' while many others felt 'we are the worst people.' What did those who were neither of these comprehend? It is a collective of a caste hierarchy enslaved because they could not adapt and assimilate according to the times. Regardless, if it is said that *Kali* is Shudra, even we do not know how we understood it. The *dharma* of *Kali*—these three eras have already functioned and passed. If any deficiency occurred in them, to rectify that flaw, the goodness of *Kali* and the Shudra must jointly attain wisdom and emerge as the authority of the *Satya Yuga*. One cannot become the authority of this *Satya Yuga* effortlessly. The intellect, capability, and competence bestowed upon us are based on an understanding of divine providence concerning us. Because we are completely unaware of it, we assume that *Kali* is evil, and it has somehow spread throughout the world as a derailed *karma*. It has been flawed over many eras. To express it in our knowledge, twenty-five *Chaturyugas* have passed since this arrived. Hence, we cannot calculate or comprehend this at all. The duration of a *Chaturyuga* is twelve thousand divine years. One divine year equates to three hundred and sixty-five human years. How can we exhaust ourselves counting this? Thus, having traversed through so many such eras, how much time do we have, at most? What are we to learn in the meantime? It is not a subject that can be completely learned. Then what must be imparted? It is the *dharma* of *Kali*. This *dharma* of *Kali* is not meant to emerge divided by caste or religion; it is a positive aspect that must manifest globally in human *dharma*. Whether you call it freedom—whatever you may designate it, no matter how much suppression was attempted, there is a transformation over the last fifty years; those up to sixty years of age can observe what that change is. Subsequent to this, the intellect of children from the last twenty years—each of you older individuals, whether it is good or bad, their intellect surpasses ours. We can discern this by observing children up to two or three years of age now. Despite such profound changes, the entire world has presented an opportunity to convince us that *Kali* is evil and *Kali* is destruction. How can this be changed? Most people presume that we cannot change it. We can change it. Therefore, this is what you must labor for. If we cannot change it, what is the benefit for our generation? We should not consider age, whether young or old. Do we need to change this or not? It absolutely must be changed. How is that possible? Within so many *Chaturyugas*, we cannot exhaustively chronicle how many millions of Mahatmas have appeared. Then how can the common populace be transformed?
Guruvani

Kalikalam: The Era of Wisdom

Seeking the virtue of a wholesome and beautiful life is a way of life for the Hindus, or what is called Sanathana. We create that virtue through our lives. Each of us grows up in such a life. This growth continued like that for a Manvanthara, or seven Manvantharas and three Chathuryugas. After that, there is an ignorance brought in the logic of the Hindus. That ignorance is that Brahman is truth and Jagat is myth. Then who should be convinced of that stage where Brahman is truth? Is it enough if Brahman is convinced? What was man made into, or what was he made into by birth in the first place, and how did the origin happen? What is the karma of that origin in the first karma? It is inside this solar system, but none of us respect it much. We all know some star for each sun and moon, and then we know the things that each great person came and did according to the Yugadharma. But we do not know when, how, and where it was done. Because of this, we have no idea what happened to us, where we went wrong, and where we did not go wrong. Why is that? It is because we do not act according to the Yugadharma. Even today, all castes and religions—at least the people in India, let alone others—are given words to believe that this is the Kaliyuga, and it will be like this- But this Kaliyuga is the time of knowledge- It is said that Kali is destruction. It is for us to acquire knowledge. This has come after many Kaliyugas and other Yugas. For this, we have had a God's grace. It is not just that, this is the time for all living people, not a caste or religion, but all castes to be liberated after living their lives in the karma of being human. You can say it in any way for that. Call it Mukthi, Moksha, or guidance, or in some other way. Or call it prophetic religion or something else. But in all these, we are seeing the karma we have worked for in some aspect. An example of that- is Wahabi's wife here? If you see them, you will not see much knowledge or familiarity. Or they have not learned to behave in the place of great knowledge. Even so, there is one thing about them. There is an issue that proves that they were able to work for a good cause in some way. But regarding us, in this lineage of ours, or in the state of a Guru lineage, or you consider it as some lineage. The Acharyas of all religions that came before this—the result of seeing God with this discriminatory mind, of all religions—are in trouble. These preachers of all religions and their followers are going into a karma that destroys themselves. There are eighty-four Nairs among the Hindus themselves; the Tamils say sixty-four Nairs. But there are eighty-four Nairs in Kerala. People do not know this. They mean Shudras. Shudra class. Those who belong to this have gone as Islam, Jain, Buddhist, and Sikh. Then no one says why this happened. If this is also said, they say they fought over caste and left. That is all they know. They do not say truly why this happened. It is precisely because they do not know that our Puranas, epics, or Shastras and religious consciousness—whichever religious consciousness you look at—are convinced by telling us completely what they saw, and telling it a little more. Because of this, we are not able to imbibe God's love, respect, or humility and make another person good. They are fighting among themselves, caught in religious consciousness and class consciousness. The example of Wahabi's wife mentioned now is proof of this. More than fifty Muslims like them are seeing this. Why is it being said? There are more Christians than that. Even people of the Sikh religion have experienced it. It has been written and sent from America. Then you do not understand what this is at all. How can I complete telling you? This is not a mischief I am doing, or any kind of miracle in it, or any kind of sleight of hand, or magic tricks to bring you closer. See what you see in the light of truth without showing what is there. Recognize what is to be known and take it. This is a big deal as far as you are entitled to it. Its necessity is the survival of man. Has man not survived till now? We do not know how far each of us has moved away in the evolution of the mistake that came in twenty-five Chathuryugas. What do you men and women who have this vision see for this? All the great ones are in front of you, giving speech to those who have got it, and at least a vision to those who have not, and leaving. They will tell those who have got speech, children, you should not make a mistake. If you make a mistake, then it cannot come back to you. Days and times will pass. You will not be able to take it either. Saying this, there are about ten, hundred, hundred and fifty people who got it that way. Even after getting all this, you do not understand. You see all religious theoreticians who are called Yogi, Karmi, Jnani, Bhakta of many kinds whom you have worshiped and whom you have never remembered doing penance. Why do they do penance? To clear up a mistake of this human world. You are seeing it yourself. Someone else is not seeing it. Seeing this, you are undertaking a great karma of bringing this to the world through your children. You may think that a magician or some theoretician saw ten or a hundred visions. But there is no use seeing a hundred or a thousand. That is not the dharma of Kali. The secret of seeing this vision is that our life did not happen today or yesterday. It is always there. You are being shown what this life has flowed through. What is being shown is its evolution. We see an arrival pattern of the sun, moon, and earth, the secret of that evolution. Apart from this, there are six spheres. It is not clear to our eyes. But the arrival nature of this and then shown to us by calculation is that this earth has to revolve around a Jupiter for twelve years. Only one revolution will come. When the earth and other moons and all this revolve for twelve years, this Jupiter comes only one revolution. We used to say such a Jupiter period. Without knowing any of this, we are connecting something. Not that, to make a correction to this, for many years, according to Brahma's decision, or how that great light is coming, we do not know, let it come anyway—we are seeing it as if it is waiting for us. This is God's love. Darshan is seeing what is the light of the life of all these human beings, how much is that stream of light, we have so many human beings here. In the life of this man, the light of that life (increases and decreases) is lost. So in order for this not to happen, God, there is a familiarity that has gone wrong for so long, as said, started working in the third Chathuryuga. Then it lay without working for three Chathuryugas. Then it started working in the seventh Chathuryuga. From then on, starting to correct, it was never possible. Thus completed the Trinity part and the Parashakti part that is said along with it in ten Chathuryugas. But what is this for, where is this culture? It is said only with three parts. That is Threthayuga and Dwapara. What is called creation karma is from an atom to the whole. If said as a whole, there is wholeness even in an atom. There is a wholeness of the world. Like this, there are many solar systems. It has a wholeness. How do we understand? Darshan is seeing and knowing this. God gave you a knowledge to say that this vision to you- some things are true in your children or father or mother. But you are not able to take this. You do not have this knowledge of how to do all that and give it to the world through our children. In that part which says to abandon everything and save your life-you don't have to abandon anything, just straighten your life. Our ancestors might have gone as ghosts, gods, sages, monks, jnanis, or bhaktas. We are seeing here the light of a great karma that needs to get liberation for all of them. So you are seeing this consciously, in dreams, in deep sleep. When we say deep sleep, we usually think of sleep. No, when our life is awake, if we close our eyes, we see. Tamil says 'Thoongamal thoongi'. It is a way of sleeping without sleeping. Even then, we are seeing this, what all it is. Like that, how many crores of great ones, sages, monks, jnanis, bhaktas, and then ordinary creatures everything. All this is showing at what time and how it was known. This is a method here. This is not something that comes if any of us think about it. That is a love of God. It has been said many times. There are men and women here who see this. From this—from your body—before this life is torn away, you are being shown what each of you has to do. Or else- there are only ten or five hundred such people. The rest are not those who see like this. But you know one thing. My father or mother did not have it. My ancestors did not have it. What is the reason for this coming to me? Where did it start? It came after we heard a method called Gurumarga. You clarify that path. That is your success. Along with clarifying this, in that ceremony where you do Gurupooja here, these manes and all that the gods worshiped have been changed and held in one place. This life is waiting to take birth through your children or your children's children. If you do not allow this, it will go and be born somewhere else where it is wrong. And it will cheat you. Gurupooja has been done. You should not go into error. It will not let go. To avoid going into this error, this event called Gurupooja was shown to you as God. But even those in your house, we did this for this, what should we do next, who should we be to each other? Let father and mother, children, husband and wife, wealth and lordship all join together. What should we become? I have not experienced till today that this thought belongs to a single household. This is my topic. Have I praised you, you have love for me, you come for prayer, you do all kinds of help and cooperation. But this is not your need. Along with saving your life, the world, for that world knowledge, how many crores of great souls, how their lives sent are standing, those with this vision are seeing. Your path is to save them. They are not the ones to play for you or for me. That is what all this has shown, what another sphere of light is doing, many of you are seeing. When you get that knowledge, if you handle it so lightly, no one can do anything. Are you going to fight and win as father, mother, and children, or are you going to take it with love, with respect, with humility—you don't know both these things. That is why I called to tell you this. I am struggling so much for this- you know that the body is not well; for that, you are also bringing prayers. But what can be done if you cannot accept this? This is not a thing that always comes in the world. It is something that has never happened since the world existed. You are seeing the birth and karma power of all religious theoreticians. Then will those children who should be respected and known come if they turn around caste and religion and fight? Or can we make those children good? How should we handle this. Think about this. You absolutely- we have done Gurupooja and this is not a big tool for everyone, it is the truth. Therefore, all of you—those who come here—this has not come like twisting and breaking the fort of magic tricks. It is said that siddhi should be pushed out like dog shit. That, even when we know about it, we ask, what is there? Is there siddhi? Or is there something else? What did you get? What ignorant things they are. They think they are going to get something. Going is not to get anything. It is to change the ignorance of his life. This Pratyaksha and Darshan or whatever synonyms there are for it, whatever it is called, all this is a tool to change this ignorance, to liberate. Each of you will become heirs of the next Yuga. Let those who say there is no birth say so. If there is no birth, then why say clairvoyant? This clairvoyant has come born and died many times. Then this karmic flaw like that stands as a big stumbling block in front of us. This must change. This is a great opportunity God has given you to change it, do not lose it. After doing Gurupooja, in your house and yours, then how many people are seen outside without doing Gurupooja. But what is the reason for all this? As long as we are alive as much as we have the right, we gain and then if God has given us birth, if He gives, whenever it is I have to liberate the life and go - it is to create this memory. This is enough for today. For this, many things have been shown here for you. Just like the locals show. School, Vanithamandalam, lifestyle for children, job, medical care—all this is being made to be done from this by including you. But you did not see any of this, nor did you hear, nor do you know. Then how will you take this? Whether you are a man or a woman who is called great, whoever you may be, if you cannot think and do like this, this will go to the verge of a great harm. It will stop only after reaching even our children. Therefore, you must be very careful and go on saying and making others say with mutual understanding. This is what I have to say.
Guruvani
