The discourse delivered by the Guru in 1993 on Guru Pooja to the workers of the Vishwa Samskarika Navothana Kendram

Certain things (the vile ones) will be destroyed keeping in mind the Deva, Yogi, Devotee, and Karmi worshipped by the ancestors. Place certain ancestors in a position fortunate enough to attain rebirth. Once other ancestors reach the status of Devas, they will hesitate to descend. A soul transforms over countless births. You should see this as a God-given path to bring about a change in the sinful and virtuous karmas of the soul, much like a tree sprouting and bearing fruit, preserving the complementary nature of the Earth, Moon, and Sun. It cannot be compared to any other ashram or system of worship. Traditional growth will occur through a girl who adheres to the truth.
If karma goes wrong without knowing what faith is, sinful forces will take hold.

The ancestors pray with the desire to take a good birth in Kali Yuga. The care of both girls and boys is essential. While living in the world, no wrong path shall be adopted. If good progeny beneficial to the home and the land are not attained, the family will be ruined. Through your life, you can attain this only through virtuous children.
To achieve the goal in mind, word, and deed, both men and women must be careful not to corrupt their special sense of imagination.
I do nothing as my own. I am merely an instrument.

It is you who must put this mission into practice. It is these good children who are gaining substance. If there is purity of character, God will also keep them close. Moving away from the karma of worshipping gods and goddesses, an opportunity is being created for them to attain liberation.
One Manvantara is twelve thousand lakh Deva years. A karma stands here convincing us that crores of births and actions are behind us.

Various methods of worship—those offering good things, those offering corrupt things—for the sake of those who worshipped associated souls and demons, Devas and ancestors are being captured, purified, and you are being saved. Accumulated karmas can be both good and bad. What is being done is opening the door to a truthful life.
A tradition that improves everything in all ways is being created. We have become recipients of the karma that obeys God's command.

Each one of you has a karma to provide a good path of life to the lineage. What is needed is the dedication and knowledge to work throughout life, compensating for the shortcomings in our souls. You are all owners of the karma to possess a life imbued with purity.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Dedication Issue 2003
It is known through experience that Kali is good, not bad

We all believe that there is a time limit for everything. However, it should be seen as a flaw that we have fallen into due to this Trimurti system, to the extent that we are unable to recognize what the dharma of Kali is. What is it? Speaking of our history, it is through the Trimurtis that we have been guided and protected. Do not assume that this Trimurti status does not exist; it does. Looking at it that way, nothing that has come up to this day is non-existent. But how do we change it? How can it be changed? Until now, anyone has only been able to dismiss it through words. No one has been able to embrace it. Then, Narayana Guru is also seen saying something like this:
The lamp that shines forth when the triad is destroyed
Cannot be attained by a false ascetic.

That is correct. How this *triputi* (threefold state) will conclude is indeed a profound subject that we must fully understand. That is Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, or Shaktheya, Shaiva, Vaishnava—this is a truth that our ancestors practiced and established. How can one say it does not exist? It certainly exists. However, although it mentions in a few words what should be done with that which exists, it is not quite like that. The aspect referred to as its knowledge is the great result of karma, executed and consolidated from within this earth, or similarly, this new age, or this new sphere. How can we reclaim it from this? It is not possible at all. The reason is not only that such a vast vision cannot be perceived, but even if it were, how and by whom could it be utilized? It is completely impossible. That is its significant peculiarity. However, our duty is to prove and make it a lived experience that this is indeed possible. Otherwise, one should not arrive at the conclusion that it does not exist, that it is non-existent, and that there is no point in anyone striving for it. It is indeed something that can be revealed and seen. Thus, when speaking of the realization of this vision, one must attain the vision of at least one *chaturyuga* (epoch of four ages). How can that be attained? Through whom can we achieve it? It would not be right to dismiss it as non-existent. In this way, various religious theorists, yogic doctrines, and numerous logical rationalizations have been combined by our people, who have said various things both in the past and the present. But they do not explain how this is to be executed. They do not know. In your experience, at least some among you sitting here—we might find at least ten or twenty people—are witnessing exactly how it is. In accordance with the *yugadharma* (duty of the age), what must come to us is the dharma of Kali. It would not be correct to say that this Kali is bad; it is good. If one asks how it can be good, our predecessors have stated it with the Guru as the witness. However, we have not understood what kind of Guru, from which era, or how they should be. Or, even if understood, the knowledge and its accompanying tradition of recitation, when fully articulated, merely become a remnant of alphabetical knowledge. How can this become the truth? How will it become true? Can one say that the karmic course of those past eras does not exist? Not at all. Furthermore, if one simply immerses and halts within the sound of Omkara, the sound 'Om' is heard in our ears for everything. That Omkara resides within us. There is a way for you to make this clear, easily clear. If you submerge in water and close both ears, you will continuously hear a humming sound of 'Om'. This exists in each of us. Therefore, one cannot simply fulfill it by explaining various meanings such as we are Brahma, or Vishnu, or Shiva. That is not the nature of this subject. In this matter, the existence culminates only in the lineage of a Guru who belongs to a karmic path where we have realized at least one *manvantara*. We consider a *manvantara* to be seventy-one *chaturyugas*. Can we complete this? That has never been possible. Nor will it be. Then, our existence is the *yugadharma* that arrives in accordance with time. That *yugadharma* is Kali. One cannot simply say that the dharma of Kali does not exist and move on. In such Kalidharma, across whatever eras you and I have repeatedly manifested, all of it is witnessed in our Guru-disciple relationship. Observing it as waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, one perceives the karma residing within ourselves in such a way that not even a hair's breadth remains to be taken. Not only that, whichever preceptors, whichever prophets, and their followers in the world have come and gone over these twenty-five *chaturyugas*, the erroneous aspects of their times are being corrected. This must happen through you yourselves. It will not be proper if it comes through the Gurus. A medium is created here for that purpose. That is why the term *Gurupooja* was mentioned. Calling it *Gurupooja* is also correct. How is that? By conceptualizing it as *Gurupooja*, envisioning their god, goddess, and ancestors, and by transforming its negative aspects, this life force is altered and stationed somewhere here. *Grihadharma* (the duty of the householder) is the reclamation of the virtuous essence of this life force. To be born into such *grihadharma*, our vision entails recognizing what great souls like these ancestors and the guidance that came through them are, and reclaiming from that. This is only possible when a Guru is present. It is the disciple themselves who perceives what such a Guru is. No one else can see it. It cannot just be taught either. Anyone can say it. Thus, it is not about whether this disciple is male or female, young or old. By showing their own dharma through themselves, pointing out whatever flaws they have, they themselves will see the Guru taking them over. This is the matter at hand. It is not about recounting miracles or great claims of mystical powers. That must not be done. If one proceeds in that manner, how many miracles can be shown to complete this? It will never work. This trinity system known to us, or the ritualistic nature of any religion—how it came about, how it can be implemented by us, and how it was implemented, is something we observe ourselves. After seeing this, they themselves will be fully convinced of what it is, within this disciple. Someone within their own family would have seen it. They are observing how that ancestor stands, how the deity stands, how the sage stands, and if there is anyone else who left as an ascetic, how they stand. Thus, we must cross at least three generations in this manner. Without this, it will not be completed. The reason for this is that one cannot just say that the karma of those living souls spanning so many *chaturyugas* does not exist. That is incorrect. How did that karma exist, and how did errors occur within it? The knowledge referred to as our *Gurupooja* must be a knowledge that corrects this. By correcting it, we are undertaking a dharma capable of attaining liberation for ourselves. This is the true path called *grihadharma*. We have often heard it said before that *grihadharma* is the greatest dharma. But what is accomplished through this *grihadharma* is what remains unknown. That is, we are reclaiming both the good and the bad of our ancestors who have come and gone over countless ages. Having reclaimed it, only the virtuous aspects are retained while the rest perishes. That must proceed within this karma of light itself. If I tell you all this right now, you might not easily grasp it. The reason is that the karmic course depicted in these trinity aspects, or in any other mythological epics, or in any other religious doctrines, stretches to a maximum of four or five thousand years. Or, if stretched further, one can tell stories, but cannot explain how it is to be corrected. So, we must reclaim it. The path of reclaiming it is what we achieve through this *grihadharma*. These steps of dharma, demonstrated and reclaimed through that *grihadharma*, must occur through a father and mother themselves. However, we have not found such parents today. Therefore, we are troubled. Now, this comes to you. Through any of those born after '73, though not in everyone, a portion of it will be fulfilled through each of them. In fulfilling this, they themselves witness the account of their births and deaths. Similarly, for it to be implemented through them, this must be seen in the special luminous form of the Guru. It will not happen simply. No matter how much one summarizes such a form of light, it cannot be articulated with a definitive conclusion or pacifying resolution. It is not like that. It must emerge through ourselves. We do not currently have parents suited for that. They are the children born after '73. For this karma to spread to those children, they themselves must see what the Guru tradition and prophetic tradition—which we have now reconstructed into temple systems and religious systems—truly are. It cannot be executed except through those who perceive this. It is approaching in this manner. Most people have felt that it is true. But crossing it is difficult. For that, our girls, or those we call mother or sister, have not reached that qualification. What about the father? Not at all. Because he was born through this mother. It won't be right. So, if asked what this mother is, we do not even know. For the position of this mother to manifest as the mother herself, there is much exertion required. Some children here have been able to see it. However, no matter what they see, say, or do, they are in a state where they leave it behind without understanding it. The very reason for that is they are people born in the astrological sign worshipped and established by their predecessors. Neither our parents nor our ancestors have the ability to liberate them from it. It is that inability that needs to be recognized by such great souls. Having been able to know this through such a great soul, we are still confused, lacking the knowledge to reclaim it today. How should we correct this? One must descend into the karma of adhering to the dharma seen through the Guru, realizing that it must be reclaimed. Another massive error has occurred among women. You know that. Even today, it exists occasionally in our country. But because it is not obvious, you are unaware of it. We send girls to the Devadasi system. It is currently somewhat detached from Kerala. Although it exists in other states, it is not explicit. This still happens in a temple in Karnataka. The state of affairs is the Devadasi system. So, the souls trapped in all these—how can this be changed? Think for yourselves. When this comes into this vision, these past karmic errors consolidated into action by gods, goddesses, sages, ascetics, and wise ones emerge before you. Must you not take this up and act upon it? What will you do for this? Through whom will it be executed? This is the issue. It cannot be suddenly explained and made understandable to someone. Or, even if you see it, you lack the karmic courage to take it up.

There are quite a few girls sitting right here. They perceive this to be the truth. However, they are unable to grasp it. This is because their life's capacity is not something that can be endured. It is an unbearable capacity. If you were to ask them how these girls came to suffer this unbearable predicament, even they would be unable to explain. Similarly, in the current scenario, there are likely at least fifteen boys present here itself.

This completely reaches a state of knowledge only along with the growth of these children. It may not be in the manner you suggest. You must observe a method for this right now. Suppose you have a five-year-old child in your home. Ascertain whether you possess the intellectual capacity that this child has at merely five years of age. If you observe them in this manner until they are about fifteen years old, you will be able to perceive it. If you look further down, what exists below the age of five is entirely different. Thus, numerous generations have passed by. Its fundamental nature involves the process of rejuvenating the souls born in previous epochs, whose karmic flaws have partially or entirely dissolved. You will not comprehend this immediately. Bringing this forth requires immense foresight from the parents, which is transmitted to these children. In this way, every child initially occupies the position of an impure entity. The mother and father must at least elevate themselves to the process of purifying this entity. Alternatively, at least the child must attain that state. Our approach entails systematically clearing the hierarchical steps of righteousness (dharma) that purify each individual. It is certainly not the knowledge constructed through the theoretical preaching of Vedanta. That knowledge represents an entirely different dimension. I am not suggesting that it does not exist. It is the intellectual knowledge of scholarly assemblies. What has this assembly been capable of achieving until today? Absolutely nothing. Apart from the mere entertainment of reciting and discussing it, nothing of substance is possible. Countless eminent figures, including Gunamkudi Masthan, Naranathu Bhranthan, and the eighteen Siddhars, have pointed out the exact same reality. However, they are unable to articulate how it should be practically executed. That remains the core issue. Therefore, you are receiving this knowledge at this juncture because it aligns with the dharma of Kali Yuga. Within the dharma of this Kali Yuga, our philosophical vision (darshana) represents the practice of eradicating the flaws of the karma performed by our ancestors, deities, and sages who operated from a detached state. That vision must inherently be realized through you yourselves. It is insufficient for the Guru merely to articulate it. What is the reason for this? What benefit do you derive if the Guru claims to have realized it? You must perceive it yourselves. You must recognize it either through the dynamic of the Guru-disciple relationship or through the karma accumulated in your previous incarnations. They must fulfill whatever that entails within the framework of the Guru-disciple relationship. You must embrace the profound dharma bestowed upon you through their children. That represents the trajectory of action intended by the dharma of a householder (Grihadharma). You may have heard this mentioned in various Puranic texts. Yet, how will it be executed? That is the crux of the matter. Consequently, when you bring this endeavor to completion—India is a relatively small nation among countries—it must necessarily be accomplished within India itself. Moreover, it must specifically occur in Kerala. This is because the central axis of India, or perhaps the world, extends downwards from Kanyakumari. Those among you who are educated are aware of this fact. There are numerous regions adjoining that central axis. It is here that its fundamental hymns of origin emerge. Grihadharma is an extraordinary constructive process of adopting those hymns of karma, transforming them into foundational steps of righteousness, turning them into sacred sanctuaries, and cultivating profound love. Through this Grihadharma, you are not meant to wander the globe; rather, God has provided you with the opportunity to take on the very existence of the world and act to harmonize it. You must recognize and undertake this yourselves. At present, it is not visible to everyone. The majority of us were born prior to the aforementioned year of 1973. Or, if born subsequently, the dominant forces are the intellectual subordinates who propagate rationalism and theories of liberation, combined with an array of absurdities. Concurrently, treating education and wealth as mere ornaments, there exist hierarchical steps of karma confined within those parameters. Having fulfilled those steps, they stand at the forefront of this paradigm. How can you possibly take this up? It is completely impossible. Therefore, when such knowledge reaches you, recognize that God has appointed you as His instruments for this specific purpose. Yet, you all presume yourselves to be insignificant, paramount, or something else entirely. Whatever aspects of this they witness, because they are born under the dominion of these deities, they are incapable of complete obedience, of carrying it forward, or of utilizing it to serve others. Such a profound ignorance remains intrinsically attached to our existence. The continuous stream of light known as Guru Dharma is what transforms this condition. The disciple must perceive the true nature of this luminous stream. It is the disciple who must meticulously categorize and integrate this, element by element. The presence of the Guru alone is inadequate. If the Guru alone executes it, it will remain flawed. Thus, this disciple embodies a dharma that remains completely impartial to distinctions of gender, stature, caste, or religion. That constitutes the true magnitude of the disciple. It attains absolute completion when it is offered back to the Guru. As long as you fail to comprehend this, neither you nor I can achieve anything of substance. This is derived from my personal experience. There were numerous followers who stood by me and experienced this reality. Yet, they too committed errors. When corrected, they persistently deviate and ultimately dissolve into obscurity. The underlying issue is that not everyone is capable of bringing it to fruition. Even upon witnessing it, they cannot internalize it. Having observed, understood, and even recognized the absolute purity of its nature, they have still strayed from the path. This constitutes our inherent karmic flaw. Rectifying this flaw is what we all collectively aspire to achieve through our household lives; furthermore, your ultimate objective is to offer this completely to the world through the emerging righteous souls and through householders who maintain unwavering vigilance. That is precisely why, when a marriage is solemnized here, the bride and groom are required to stay at the premises for approximately a week. Some, according to their own volition, choose to remain for a month or even a month and a half. Such profound wisdom is embedded within this practice. God has graciously granted us an era wherein we can reclaim this wisdom through our descendants. It must be noted that this practice is predominantly beneficial for families who have conducted Guru Pooja here and subsequently arrange marriages through this institution, recognizing its inherent value. Conversely, if parents independently arrange a marriage based solely on their personal preferences, the intended purpose will not materialize. What is the underlying reason? The familial environments of the bride and the groom will fundamentally lack compatibility. Even if they temporarily align, they will fail to nurture it with genuine love. They will remain completely entangled in karmic afflictions capable of alienating the bride and groom entirely. What assistance can we offer them? We can do absolutely nothing.

Everyone knows the difficulty of raising a child, whether male or female. In any case, they do not raise them to kill and eat them. They will do various things according to the desires of those who raise them. But it does not materialize. Why ? Because of our previously acquired *karmadosha*, we tend to stray like this. Therefore, it is that very *karmadosha* that made this person refuse to agree. That is an experience in that house itself. This is what we must understand. Can they ever return to that house? You might think that if one possesses education, wealth, and intellect ٹ..!

We are the people whom God has given an opportunity to accomplish this. By guiding each of us towards the aspect called the Guru, reclaiming that *karma* and realizing the *dharma* of the world, imparting it to the children, and putting it into practice, the parents will attain the very position that the child reaches. This is what I have to say.
Guruvani
Santhigiri Janmadinapoojitha Commemorative Edition 2003
The fallacies brought about by worship and other aspects

We have an acquaintance that is ignorant of how this Trimurti worship came about, how it will eventually fade, or how it is currently sustained. Over time, lower-level cultures have increased, and for the past three hundred years, this worship has existed in a state of profound ignorance. Our Karunagappally and Karthikappally fall into this category. The story of Ochira is narrated in a similar vein. So, what we have witnessed is the manifestation of the deity and its subsequent transformation. Then comes the aspect of *Siddhi* (special powers). These deities, goddesses, and spirits will suddenly display miraculous tests. We mistakenly assume that these phenomena originate from God. Would God display such things before us? We have heard that because the lineage of Manu took the wrong turn, a curse was pronounced by Brahman back then. Only we believe this; no one else in the world has heard of it. The reason attributed to this is that from the moment this *Chaturvakyam* (four profound utterances) emerged, divine grace was lost. Divine grace means the grace of Brahman. It is not something possessing form or name. The Trimurti system originated after this grace was lost and the *Chaturyuga* remained inactive. When the Trimurti system reached its completion, the fourth face was missing. That is why the very name 'Nanmukhan' (the four-faced one) was lost. Consequently, it is this three-faced system that was finalized. Therefore, the completion of this three-faced system does not belong to the tradition of Manu. It was established as Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva—or as Shaktheyam, Shaivam, and Vaishnavam—and all aspects of good and evil were concealed beneath it. What did you understand? If this befell the Hindus first, it has subsequently affected the entire world. This is precisely what others state as well. Concepts like Adam, Allah, and the Holy Spirit reflect how this has permeated all other religions. However, people remain unaware of this truth. Consider the crores of people practicing this—over a hundred years, countless millions have been absorbed into this system! It has since evolved into various religious doctrines in multitude of ways. Who can truly comprehend this, and how? Can this be understood through Puranas and Epics, or by interpreting the meaning of the Upanishads? How can one grasp this merely by preaching and practicing the essence of the Vedas? Some among you, both men and women, hold such perspectives. But what have you actually understood? Speak for yourselves. I have pointed out this experience among us on numerous occasions. What we term Hinduism today is a lineage where the Trimurti system was reiterated after the *Manusmriti* or the Manu lineage went astray. Furthermore, since we cannot distinguish whether it is Hindu or Sanatana, if we ask the Brahmins, they will claim to be Sanatanis. How can one be a Sanatani while worshipping the Trimurti? It is impossible. Consequently, they perished. Today, those Brahmin families and anyone who followed this Vedic law have met their downfall. Subsequently, many individuals, looking mechanically towards the West and accumulating degree after degree, will travel wherever necessary abroad for employment. In reality, they possess no genuine connection with their families. This is the kind of tradition they have inherited. When did the entire Shudra class assimilate among you?

You cannot say anything about what its realization is, other than saying that we follow the Guru's path, whether you call it Gurupooja or anything else ٹ to tell . This is what happens from Sri Krishna's time until today; apart from making up stories by combining many men and women while talking about Sri Krishna, if asked what you have understood about Sri Krishna, what will you say? Even that is not understood . After this , the knowledge we have received about those who came after Sri Krishna till today is of 2,444 great souls. Their capability has also reached this lineage . So all of them have come together, and their disciples, or everything that came in the nature of their worship, should merge and dissolve into the lineage. How did you understand that? Their liberation. What should you get from it? That soul breaking away all the evil it has acquired till today - this is breaking away through the Guru ٹ in a thousand ways for a thousand people ٹ and for lakhs of people ٹ this is being broken. That light shines, and you are seeing it. It has brought us to the forefront of many karmas. This is for all children as well. Someone might think what they got is right. It is not like that . Then some education or knowledge might have come in the model of a house. I have said many times why this is given through women. If their two generations do not grow , by two generations it means one generation is a hundred and twenty years. Within these a hundred and twenty years, there will be very few like the mother. The rest must be done by their children and their children's children. Should we implement this through them or not? How will that be implemented? Tell me what your knowledge is.

It is in the Trimurti tradition that our worship has been conducted till today , as far as we know. Right? But that is not our system of worship. Manvantaram ٹ That is the 28th Chaturyuga of the seventh Manu after the Manvantaram. In this yuga , to us, in this Manvantaram , it was a mistake made by some Guru . It is a mistake . Not a lack of knowledge . We are uprooting the basis of that mistake . How do we uproot it? Saying a word wrong will cause harm. This lineage of ours will be deprived of it. By lineage, it does not mean everyone will be deprived of it , but at least a few will miss out on it. They are the ones who reject it despite knowing it. Doing this Guru Puja according to our understanding and as guided by God, is to set aside ancestors, deities, and everything like them. This must henceforth be born in your lineage. It should be born as a Guru parampara (lineage of Gurus). And not as a deva parampara (lineage of deities) or any other--like Shaktheya, Shaiva, or Vaishnava --lineage . We are taking hold of all these three. We have taken hold of them. It was on the day we took hold of them that Guruvayur caught fire. After that, we endured great sorrow for six or seven years for it to be fulfilled. It has been about fifteen years since it was fulfilled. After this, apart from the family who performed this Guru Puja, if there is any family entitled to it, not just in our Kerala or India, but anywhere in the world, it ٹ.

This was not obtained for nothing. You are the ones who, at some point in time, desired this in some way of life. Then it faded away. After losing it, you entered into this Trimurti system. It is not something recent. To destroy this entirely, who is there? The Guru. How does the Guru destroy it? You know this is the truth. But you neither desire it in the same way, nor do you accept it. Ancestors from countless crores of past lives have been sent across! About a hundred among those of you who came that day have witnessed it like that. This is what is said to have started from Kanyakumari. I have told you a historical truth regarding this. You do not know how to accept it. Kanyakumari is the place where the equator converges, isn't it? The equator. It begins from Kanyakumari and a central part of the Indian Ocean. Then you learn another name as well. The name of a rock is mentioned there, right? Mainakam. It is from there that this originates. That is why the Gandhi Ghat was placed there. Do you ever think about any of this? Aren't you educated people? If you don't do this, what will you do? From there, our equator passed. It goes towards Germany, doesn't it? It is in this region that the light remains. It has appeared right in the middle of the Indian Ocean. It has emerged in a history where the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea, and the Indian Ocean—all three blend together. Having received this, what have you been able to do? You are the ones who study and teach this history. This history merely provides a subtle sign in the place where such history is being studied. Apart from narrating this history like this, none of us knows anything. The greatness of India remains unknown. People from outside say that they wish to be born in India at least as a blade of grass. Therefore, this land that has attained such immense greatness, especially Kerala. The origin of Kerala is Kanyakumari. It was received there. We have been there and experienced it as well. You remember, don't you? Thus, this is a time ordained for you by God.

The Trimurti system, after this mistake of the Manu lineage, was completed in ten Chaturyugas. Out of that, three Chaturyugas remained inactive. Then it started functioning from the fourth Chaturyuga. Thus, it actually functioned from the seventh Chaturyuga. This Trimurti system was completed in the seventeenth Chaturyuga. Nothing has happened beyond this. Crores of humans have come. The birth of Sree Rama happened for that purpose. It is said that it came about because Vashistha performed the Putrakameshti ritual. Even that was not complete. Now, having crossed everything, it has arrived after this Kaliyuga has completed five thousand years. This is the resource you have received. How did you get this? How did these devas, devis, rishis, sanyasis, and jnanis—crores of them—get it? Why did they get it? Why don't you think like that? How will you understand this? It is something that cannot be attained even after striving for crores of births. That is why it is said, 'Yatra yatra Yogeshwara Krishna'. Even those who came like that could not achieve this. This is abundantly available to you. However a human life has been stacked and accumulated, those sins and merits are given to you after being completely destroyed in this light. You must understand that. This is a truth received for your family life or for completing a human life. If you do not understand this truth, you will never get it in another birth. It is just that you do not receive it in the same way. You receive it in a manner akin to the saying 'a thousand ways for a thousand people'. Women should nicely merge their prayers, intentions, knowledge, acquaintance, and all thoughts and emotions into those lotus feet and shouldn't you have at least a thought that you are being saved from it? Isn't that what you need? All the flaws of these women are removed, and if they have a husband, wife, and children, through their intentions and prayers, Narayana Guru says thus: 'Bharya Bhajati Bhartaram'. Even if the husband becomes ignorant, through the knowledge of this wife, he will at least attain moksha. And not mukti. This is how it is stated. So, even after so many of you have seen it, honoring that, shouldn't you have at least the knowledge that 'for my house, for my children, for my husband'? Knowing that, shouldn't you explain this to your children saying, 'Children, this is the greatest in the world, the first karma' ٹ You should explain and make them understand this.

You, who have this much knowledge, must think about how you should receive this. In the realm of knowledge, it is a traditional path that equally accepts the rights and wrongs of human life. This is the first of its kind in the world. Shouldn't you have the wisdom to respect and accept it? There is no one ready to take this up. My body - even lying down like this, I am speaking. What should each of you do? These people standing near me right now, each one of them, if they are like this, then what can I do? Realizing it as a memory, you must understand and act according to your knowledge as needed. This should traditionally reach the world as your acquired karma. You must understand and act accordingly. What can I do? I am not putting on any pretense before you. You would have shown greater respect than this. I know a trick. Do you know what it is? Forcefully pushing it upon you. And then lining up ten or a hundred people, praising them as 'he' and 'him' and parading them around, just ordinary people. Hearing this, you would tremble and accept it. But that is deceit. Nothing can be gained through that deceit. What can be done if those without devotion are caught in this blindness? So, this is entirely a provision given to you by God. If you harbor jealousy, darkness, or ignorance towards this, the same will happen to your entire household. We do not belong to any caste or religion. This holds the highest and most formidable position in the human world. You should understand and do this. You must know this. Grieving with our minds, whatever needs to exist in this world is bestowed upon us through that supreme cosmic power. What should we do? I do not know, dear. You must submit this request and take it up. Otherwise, there is no point in us merely repeating this as a model.

If our boys are not capable of taking this up, it is to be attained through women. Women must fully reflect that image of the primordial mother. The coming generationٹ from them, along with their husbands and children, are meant for serving the world. For this, you must see one thing: whatever exists in the world will be shown. Then each of the spheres will be shown. In a way that proves that the Guru stands with you, or else, Asan says like this, "He sees without eyes, hears without ears" -- this is the part which says that. Kumaran Asan says this. Even though all these things were said, it was said as a continuation of learning due to the Guru's approach. But no one was able to grasp it. Then for that characteristic, many ways have been mentioned. Such a person walks devoid of illusions and desires, as an Atmayogi. These illusions and deceptions are of no consequence to him. What else? Like a madman. What is madness? Craziness. Being mad means those who lack sense in their heads. Like a madman, like an absolute simpleton - like someone who knows nothing, walking devoid of illusions, desires, and magic, an Atmayogi - this is what Asan said. That is the practice of an Avadhuta. But it is fulfilled exactly as you see it. So wherever the Guru's light exists, in that light, this path of karma, as a mother, where do you take it -- that is what is seen. So, given to you by God is a great light of truth! You were called to be told this. Even if we didn't know it, we were able to come this way and understand that this is the truth. Now you are the ones who must think about what to do with it. Not me. I should not tell you anything more for this. Because based on what you see, you are the ones who must decide to change these deceptions of the world. For that, is there any need to think about things caused by our ignorance and sit behind them grieving about it?

Is our life not one born under the influence of the twenty-seven constellations? It should align with the calculation of three zodiac signs. Three times nine is twenty-seven. Over how many tens of millions of lifetimes might we have been connected to those who fall under these? There will be wicked individuals, malicious ones, and those who have harmed us in every conceivable manner. Encountering them evokes feelings of affection, resentment, and goodness within us. This is the inherent play of it. I shall limit my words to this for the time being.

This is the contribution imparted to the world through you and your lineage. In the capacity of a mother, this is sequentially inherited by the mother, the children, and so forth. Where else does such a phenomenon occur? Having received this, our duty is to preserve and dignify it, thereby conferring dignity upon the world and inspiring its adoption. It is not something to be merely observed and discarded; it is not akin to visiting a museum and returning. We are earnestly seeking this through our very existence. This is not an instruction for you to embrace asceticism (*sannyasa*). Asceticism is an entirely distinct path. What is being expounded here transcends asceticism profoundly. It is not mere renunciation. It is a divine manifestation brought forth by the will of God for the entire world. That is precisely what must be comprehended.

Consider the elderly mothers of our past—those who frequented the markets. They are unique to this region of South Travancore. Have you observed them placing another basket inside a torn fish basket and carrying it upon their heads? Similarly, this is an inadvertent error that has occurred. It is a provision graciously bestowed upon us by God. It must not be discarded. This is the only counsel I have. Through the actions you perform and inspire here, and through your words imbued with greatness, all those who come and go must be uplifted. Everyone who visits this place and departs must attain a profound sense of peace and tranquility.
Guruvani
October 2003

I have visited on numerous occasions. Each time, I would come as far as Olassery and then return. I had not ventured into other nearby localities, having visited merely two or four places. Never before have I come here during this summer season. I was told that this is a remarkable place. Somehow, a synthesis of the land's ancient and modern knowledge has merged here. However, we have not been able to assimilate it in the proper manner, nor have we had the opportunity to do so. If one asks whether it is better elsewhere, the answer is no. The reason for this lies in our archaic knowledge and familiarities—what constitutes the distinction between the lineage of the Trimurti and that of Manu, what Manu represents, and how Manu came to be. We have not been corrected or enlightened regarding such profound knowledge. There is another reason to state for this. We acquire complete knowledge of the divine will only from certain transcendent Gurus of different eras and their contemporary counterparts. However, the prevailing understanding is that this knowledge slipped from our grasp approximately twenty-five *Chaturyugas* ago. This cannot be comprehended through the words of ordinary mortals, nor can it be realized through the words of deities. I acquired this knowledge much like one learns through an unforeseen ordeal. If you ask how, we once possessed a certain knowledge—a knowledge belonging to the lineage of the Trimurti. Customarily, it elaborates on the aspects of *Parashakti* and then concludes there. Or, to express it in a slightly more refined manner, we have only witnessed the practice of narrating the tale of Devendra and then casually dismissing it as the divine play of the Lord. In all those instances, we are presented with acts that merely evoke astonishment. We are left with no choice but to blindly believe. Why? Because we were unaware of where the error lay and where it required correction. I indicated to you earlier that this was realized through being caught in such a misconception. This so-called misconception is evident in the fact that we observe a deeply entrenched familiarity with vehemently worshipping actions up to the stature of the Trimurti. Yet, this essentially halts with forceful narrations of the heavenly realms. To reconcile this, we are appeased with descriptions of the 'netherworld' (*Pathala*), accompanied by its specific attributes. When patched together with aspects of the dharma of *Kali Yuga*, it never truly aligns logically. As they narrate this, we are taught and made to recite tales of realms that could merely be rationalized as the other side of our earth. Nevertheless, this does not elevate us to a genuine state of profound knowledge. It fails to transcend the boundaries of a merely geographically expansive understanding. The reason it fails to transcend is because it is a narrative constructed by referencing the positions of Devendra and Parashakti, and writing further based solely upon them. It neither progresses beyond that point, nor is it possible to even reach thus far. Subsequently, this is how we perceive it. We note that certain *Puranas* delineate transitional states of existence. However, they have been unable to conclusively explain them. What does this mean? When we speak of a transitional state, it is essentially a vision or revelation. The definitive conclusion of this vision is stated precisely in terms of seven thousand, seven thousand four hundred and forty-four, and so on—incrementing by seventy to reach seventy thousand seven hundred and forty-three. Consequently, this implies that such a multitude of transitional states exist within a specialized framework of completion. How can we demonstrate this? In what manner can it be articulated? However, this vision is exceedingly rare for an ordinary human to attain. Even if attained, we are scarcely permitted to fully immerse ourselves in it. The reason is that Gurus who have transcended this fourth state are exceedingly rare. The designation of *Hamsa* has been appended—many Gurus are referenced with this title—yet we have not been informed of the various categories of this *Hamsa* state. Everything is simply stated by attaching the term *Hamsa*. To summarize this *Hamsa* state, once we began discussing it, it was postulated that, if necessary, all animals serve as the vehicles for these incarnate beings. How many can realistically believe this? Similarly, we remain stagnated at a point where we are merely told of the vehicle of Subrahmanya or the vehicle of Garuda. This is a domain where they have meticulously managed the convergence of the material and the spiritual. Yet, upon reaching that juncture, they find themselves with nothing substantive to impart. This is my personal experience. The reason they lack anything to impart is that some of us have heard up to what extent this status of Devendra reaches, though not everyone has. The entity known as Devendra is one who has surpassed this status of *Deva*. If it is concluded with the tale of a *Yaksha*, and we are told this is not it, we would fail to comprehend it. Because we have neither witnessed it, nor has it been explained to us. And if asked what has been explained, we remain ignorant of that as well. It is only after being trapped and wandering for an immeasurable epoch in the deeds where the *Puranas* and epics ultimately culminated, that we are finally granted an opportunity to emerge from it. Regarding this, the epochs articulated by the author of the *Gita* are indeed the accurate ones.

In that position referred to as 'Kali Shudrankal' (Kali in the Shudra), it is the Shudra class. When we speak of the Shudra class, in our Kerala itself, it has been divided into seventy-four castes. These seventy-four castes, when they reach North India, transform into more than a hundred. We cannot even imagine where this sense of dharma—which subsequently turned caste into a deity and rendered it devoid of karma—will take us, how it will culminate, and how we will be able to proceed. The reality is that no Purana, Itihasa (epic), or Shastra has emerged to explain how we should overcome such karmic defects. Why did it not emerge? It is because of not acting with the knowledge of the times (Yugas). When we speak of times, we are thinking about the four epochs: Satyayuga or Kritayuga, Tretayuga, Dwapara, and Kali. We have arrived at the point where the author of the Gita has stated 'Kali Shudrankal'. Thus, standing here, like those who are unable to comprehend the interpretation concerning us without a completely theoretical knowledge or without learning a language, which guru—who is the guru of these times, why are the primordial gurus mentioned in this way to merely gloss over things, who should come as the followers of this guru, in which lineage should it culminate, which part should it reach—this is what we do not know. So, what is the dharma of Kali? We ourselves must observe the rights and wrongs that have occurred up to this day. Having seen that, we should fulfill it within the dharma of Kali. It is not about running away and abandoning Kali. We have been made to believe that the dharma of Kali is entirely evil. Because Kali has been depicted as a defect in this manner, we do not become thinkers in every way. Then, one should not think about it. It is said what state is achieved in that experience by placing atomic science in it through an atmospheric revolution. But beyond that, no one can do anything there. Knowing how this atom originated is the path. What this path implies is, how does the vibration of an atom exist within us? How many billions of vibrations exist together? It means we must perceive this ourselves. There is no other justification. Discovering it in this manner, if we say male and female, it is sufficient to view it merely as an origin. Be it male or female, or any other prophetic religion, or any other kind of guru across times (Kalanthara Guru), they cannot just depart after merely receiving vibrations corresponding to that epoch. But even if they receive it, they do not become a Kalanthara Guru. The description of an epoch is illustrated through twenty-one gurus. So, in reality, we have not been able to see such gurus anywhere recently. If there are any, it is the misfortune of not being able to transition through there. That is what is called a Yogi. So, what has the Yogi done? He will not touch anyone. Without touching anyone, proceeding along a path, mastering the laws of this nature in whatever ways possible, and considering this law as his life, he preserved it as Yoga.
Guruvani
October 2003

I have come many times. During all those times, I would come up to Olassery. And then return. I haven't traveled to other nearby areas. I have only visited two or four places. I haven't come here during this summer season. It was said that this is a special place. An old and new knowledge of the land has somehow merged into this. But we haven't been able to embrace it in the appropriate way. We haven't had the opportunity for that either. If asked whether it is better anywhere else in other aspects, that is not the case either. The reason for this is that we have not been corrected in the knowledge regarding what our outdated understanding and familiarity are, the difference between the Trimurti lineage and the Manu lineage, what Manu is, and how Manu came into being. Another reason to state for that is this: we come to fully know about the divine resolve from some Kalanthara Guru (guru across times) and the contemporary gurus associated with them. But the knowledge is that this slipped out of our hands approximately twenty-five Chaturyugas (four-epoch cycles) ago. This cannot be comprehended by humans speaking of it. It cannot be comprehended by a Deva speaking of it either. I came to know of it just as one realizes something by getting into an accident. If asked how, we possessed a certain knowledge; a knowledge belonging to the Trimurti lineage. The custom is to state the matters of Parashakti and stop right there. Or, to articulate it in a slightly more refined manner, the only application we have witnessed is narrating the story of Devendra and dismissing it by saying it is the play of the Lord. Everywhere there, a karma that creates wonder is what has been presented to us. We can only believe it. Why? It is because we reached a point of not knowing where the error occurred and where it needs to be corrected. I indicated to you that this was realized by falling into this blunder. What is referred to as this blunder is that we observe a familiarity of having worshipped most powerfully the karmas up to the Trimurti status. But this also strongly narrates the story of the heavenly world and halts. To justify that to us, they mention 'Pathalanagaram' (the netherworld city) and narrate its special features. That never aligns correctly when juxtaposing certain things with the dharma of Kali. When they come around to stating this, we have learned by being told and made to recite matters of countries that can be passed off as being on the far side of this earth. But because of this, we do not reach the threshold of knowledge either. This does not transcend beyond a nationwide knowledge. The reason it does not cross over is the karma written and linked by mentioning the Devendra status and Parashakti status. It does not evolve beyond that either. But it is not possible to arrive here either. Then this is how we perceive it. We mention states of transition (avasthantharabhdham) in some Puranas. But they haven't been able to articulate it conclusively. What is it? When we speak of states of transition, it is a vision. The resolution of this vision is stated entirely as seven thousand, seven thousand four hundred and forty-four, adding seventy like that, to seventy thousand seven hundred and forty-three. So, it implies there are this many states of transition in a specific culmination. How will we demonstrate this? In what manner can it be explained? But this vision is attained by a common man only as a rarity. Even if attained, we will not be permitted to enter into it. The reason for that—the gurus who have transcended this fourth stage are exceedingly few. Hamsapadam (the state of the swan) is appended to everything, many gurus are mentioned by associating it like that—we haven't been informed what all categories of Hamsapadam it entails. Everything is stated by appending Hamsa. To provide a summary of this Hamsapadam, we started articulating it and, if necessary, all animals are designated as the vehicles of these avatars. How many people can believe this? Similarly, we do not reach anywhere except a position glossed over, such as the vehicle of Subrahmanya or the Garuda vehicle. This is a realm they have carefully navigated by intertwining the material and the spiritual. But upon reaching there, they have nothing to impart. This is an experience of mine. The lack of anything to impart arose; some of us have heard to what extent this Devendra status reaches. Not everyone has heard. The individual named Devendra is one who has transcended this Deva status. By concluding it with the story of a Yaksha, and stating this is not it, we wouldn't comprehend it either. Because we haven't witnessed it, nor has it been conveyed to us. But if asked what has been conveyed, we do not know that either. In the karma where the Puranas and Itihasas have arrived in this manner, after revolving within it for so long, an opportunity is obtained to emerge from it. For this, the times mentioned by the author of the Gita are what is accurate in it.

In that position known as 'Kali in Shudra', it is the Shudra class. Thus, when we speak of the Shudra class, even in our Kerala, they have been divided into seventy-four castes. These seventy-four castes become more than a hundred when we go to North India. We cannot even imagine where this sense of dharma—which has later turned into a deity of caste and rendered actionless—will take us, how it will end, or how we will be able to proceed. The reality is that neither a Purana, nor an epic, nor a science has arrived to articulate how we should redeem ourselves when caught in such a flaw of karma. Why did it not arrive? It is because they do not function with the knowledge of times. What we consider as 'times' refers to the four epochs: Satya Yuga or Krita Yuga, Treta Yuga, Dvapara, and Kali. We are now standing at the juncture where the author of the Gita mentions 'this Kali in Shudra'. Thus standing here, like those who lack absolute theoretical knowledge or who cannot comprehend interpretations without studying a language, what we do not know is: who are the gurus? Who is the guru of these times? Why are the primeval gurus merely invoked for the sake of it? Who should become the followers of this guru? In which lineage should it culminate, and which part should it reach? What, then, is the dharma of Kali? We ourselves must observe the rights and wrongs that have occurred to date. Having seen that, we must fulfill it within the dharma of Kali, rather than running away from Kali. We have been made to believe that the dharma of Kali is entirely flawed. Because Kali has been depicted as an evil, we do not become thoughtful in every aspect. Furthermore, one should not think about it. It describes what state is experienced by incorporating atomic science into atmospheric revolution. But beyond that, no one can do anything there. Knowing how this atom originated is the way. Regarding this way, how does the vibration of an atom exist within us? How many billions of vibrations exist together? It means that we ourselves should perceive this. There is no other logic. After discovering this in such a way, we only need to view men and women merely as an origin. It is impossible for a man and a woman, or any prophetic religion, or any guru of the era for that matter, to simply depart after acquiring only the vibrations corresponding to that era. But acquiring it does not make one a guru of the era. The description of an era is illustrated through twenty-one gurus. However, we have not actually been able to see such gurus anywhere recently. Even if they exist, it is a misfortune that one cannot reach out to them. That is what is called a yogi. So, what has the yogi done? He touches no one. Going along a path without touching anyone, he mastered the laws of this nature in whatever ways possible, considered these laws as his life, and preserved it as yoga.
Guruvani
November 2003

Therefore, he can never grow and arrive with wealth and prosperity. Buddha is an evidence of this. Another evidence is Sri Shankara. Observe where these two reached by taking two different paths. The numerous gurus who came after Sri Krishna are the evidence. All of them acted with the desire to speak the truth in various things. But they did not reach it. This is what you must see. The prophetic religions and they too have arrived at this same point by saying various things. So, if this prophetic religion is stated to be wrong, how can another person's religion be right? It is fine if it changes by being proven wrong. Alternatively, if other paths of the gurus are stated to be wrong, how can one say that any other guru's path is right? So, whatever rights and wrongs have occurred to date, the first question is: what is the cause for this? We must thoroughly understand and describe those effects that originated from that cause. By describing and understanding them thus, making the children investigate what this mentioned path is, and as parents, knowing and understanding that path ourselves, how can we bring about a change from the flaw of karma where one has transformed into a deva, a devi, a rishi, and a sanyasi? That is not possible if only a man changes or if only a woman changes. For this, one must reach at least the position of Vashistha or Vyasa, who advised the devas. If you stay away saying that this is a very lengthy matter, you will not attain it. This is an era where either a woman or a man can utilize the dharma of Kali. You should never consider it as a caste or a religion.

We have been born in the dharma of Kali in order to take up and execute a dharma that entirely belongs to the human world. We must inevitably reach this. Even if we happen to be born out of this time, it will not be possible. Every era has its own special mandate. Having been born in Kali, how can we proceed without respecting it by saying that Kali is bad? Therefore, we can only proceed by respecting Kali. How should it be respected? What should we be like in order to respect it? How are the chronicles of these past times narrated? Such matters have been stated to some extent through Puranas or epics. But when it comes to reality, they mislead. This has been our experience till date. To deviate from this, many gurus and prophets have been brought into this dharma of Kali Yuga over various times since Sri Krishna. Thus, in between, great sages have also been brought to provide guidance to this deva and devi. But we do not know how this guidance is provided to the deva and devi. Then, all we know is that going somewhere according to this Amavasya—most people do not do it, but when a few go for the bali ritual—various phrases are recited there. "Anya janmane bandhavah" is a word uttered at the very end. So, will everything be resolved just by saying this?

Will it be resolved if we repeatedly say all these things starting with 'Jambu Vivekanandavarshe'? Therefore, this is not it; regarding us, where did this flaw of karma occur—this is what needs to be known. But it will not work even if a man and a woman know it separately. This is because, as long as the father, mother, and children do not unite, you cannot do anything. This is the result of your united actions as father, mother, children, husband, and wife.

You must start your ascent from wherever you attain the grace of a Guru. Otherwise, when we speak of working together, is anyone acting without cooperation? No. Each of us is the creator of an idea that remains unsatisfied no matter how much wealth, power, and knowledge we acquire. Where can we find a change from this? Change cannot be obtained from anywhere. So, the knowledge we have been led to believe is that one should embrace renunciation after wandering in pursuit of this until three-quarters of life is over and the strength of the nerves has waned. When these nerves are in a state where they cannot even be lifted, what can possibly be accomplished here? We are drowning in a sense of Dharma that has fallen into the ocean, merely trying to discover in which era of the epics and Puranas some knowledge from an unknown time was preserved. We must step away from this. To step away from this, a proof is needed. I am trying to explain it briefly here. It is impossible to study and teach the glories of all the Gurus and prophets who have appeared to date, the apostles who came as their followers, or the disciples of the Gurus who belong to these four realms. Instead, we are discovering it. Discovering it means recovering it from the great sin of a Guru's sacrifice—what is meant by the great sin of sacrifice? When one goes to immerse oneself in sacrifice, everyone rejects him like a great sinner. People will never be found to love him. When he remains unloved in this way, his mind will wander in the tragic state of being unable to connect with and love anyone. It is the same whether it is a man or a woman. Furthermore, if one receives one, two, ten, or a hundred visions, they will keep diverting us by showing the conditions of these visions. So, if the conditions of the vision keep diverting us, how will we search for and find it? Which is right and which is wrong—there are no two paths for men and women for this. There is only one path. Then on this path, in the characteristic of the Yogi who said that women—even one's mother—should not be in the house, in this conditioned karma where one attains proficiency in action, who can remove the karmic flaws of a human life that has fallen and struggled, and how? Or if someone is called a perfect devotee, how can one know what that devotee truly is? It is never possible. Because, to hasten toward the realm called the Guru, one must know what a Deva is, what a Devi is, what a demon is, or what is the significance of the epochs that have evolved from a worm or even an atom? This is impossible for anyone other than a Guru who can reveal this. So how do we know what kind of a Guru that is?

There is a meaning that we have been taught. What is it? How will we survive in an era that dictates even mothers, who are women, are restricted? Or suppose someone goes out alone and achieves something. Isn't it an act of destroying people by reaching the realm of magical powers and performing miracles? Thus, attaining all kinds of occult powers and letting them overflow as if they were true wisdom is the karmic flaw that has afflicted us. When we hear 'Siddhi' (occult power), we think of a wise person. There are many Siddhis. Even manifesting a lower spirit (Chathan) is said to require eighteen siddhis. Man calls even this Chathan or Madan 'Lord'. And then this sorcerer or the so-called Vaidika tells us: Madan, Nadan, Nadesan. Meaning, Madan grew up to become Nadan and transformed into Nadesan. If we are made to believe that this Nadan has such abilities, where will we fall following this path? Where will we end up? How will we proceed? We have fallen into the midst of such a karmic affliction. So, having spoken about Sri Krishna and brought him through two paths, why wasn't this Sri Krishna kept in our land? What is the reason for him going outside India? When he went somewhere, gathered everything, and built a life there, what caused it to sink in the water? Such a habit of thinking does not even occur to us - or even if we did think, there is no way to find out regardless of whom we ask. Then, although some things have been agreed upon in certain places, implementing them is difficult. What is it? Now, Sree Narayana Guru, Chattampi Swami, or Sree Sankara - these three great men were born in Kerala. Saying it is Adi Sankara whom they knew and reached, what is the path we have arrived at? Does our nature only have the measure of these thousand years? If we rely on Adi Sankara, who did not understand any of this, as a reporter, how can we move forward? We shouldn't seek understanding through that path. How has it completely changed for us over the preceding ages? What all happened due to the progression of those times? Where do we and our ancestors stand after living through such a long period - this is the grace of the Guru. We cannot move forward from where those ancestors stand. We cannot abandon them on the way either. We can only move forward after performing ancestral purification, divine purification, or even the sage-level purification associated with them. If asked how to purify them, it is through the colors of light. So, having perceived this light-color, how is the Guru-essence that has taken form in it, what paths did the Guru who took that form travel, was it a Guru who lived by blending Karma, Yoga, Jnana, and Bhakti to attain karmic fitness, or someone who came as an heir, established the Guru Dharma and departed, or someone who reached the level of qualities that should exist in a Guru but couldn't act - when such a state of ignorance has pervaded our scientific understanding and epics, and we say we are completely lost, it is not merely the state of the place and time, but the state of the space and time of the ages. For a certain period, we completely cannot act. Why? Where it is calculated that a Kali Yuga itself spans four hundred and thirty-two thousand years, our subject is to understand by analyzing the Kali eras that have been estimated at five thousand years, a special rule. That is what we must understand. How will we perceive this? We can never see it. But then again, we can. There is no point in insulting anyone by speaking about something that doesn't exist. Or there is no point in saying it even if one's intellect has developed. For that, a soul suited for your attainment of a Guru must be a Guru who reveals what you and your lineage are. The karmic capacity to bond with that soul is called our inherent tendency (vasana), and it serves that purpose. That is the vasana of the soul. How that soul operates within these universal elements and the five senses and culminates in the five sheaths. The Guru is the one who integrates the dharma of karma and vikarma acting as the living being and the soul through these five sheaths and reveals it here. Otherwise, that Guru cannot be attained for trivial matters. So, if you are told this, where will you end up standing? You should view it like this. I told you that I arrived here by mistake. Because once we have become fully capable up to the Trinity system, what do we think? That if we mention the Trinity, we don't need to seek anything else. There is indeed such a time. I won't deny it. That period is after completing the Treta Yuga and up to the end of the Dvapara Yuga. After that, there is no point looking there. This culminates in Krishna. That story of Krishna is what I narrated earlier. When it stops at Krishna, how will we know the nature of the Gurus who came later? How will we understand what exists within those Gurus? That is something shared mutually by the disciple and the Guru. The author of the Gita describes it as the discrimination between the Self and the non-Self, cultivated by men and women, young and old, according to their respective merits. It is discerning the Self through the Self. Then how much merit from past lives is required? This is it. It is the Guru who must account for it. Thus, counting and reaching the karma where the counted number becomes meaningful, we are observing this. What all is it? It involves showing us the time from which these elemental forces began to move and act. There should never be a deviation from that. If it changes, it is lost. If we introduce a change and reach there, it will be akin to trying to extract the core of a banyan tree. It will be like searching for the core of a banyan tree that has been spreading branch after branch for thousands of years. That is not how a meaning is assigned to this banyan tree. How its veins flow, how it draws nourishment from the tip of the leaf, that is the only cause. So, just as a tree does not grow without leaves or its other characteristics, man has grown and become an entity devoid of a core. But there is a core. Where does it merge? It merges when the karma to attain Advaita dissolves upon realizing what exists in the eighth realm above these seven realms. That is how karma ceases to remain there. Otherwise, denying the existence of karma will bring us harm. Thus, through how many variations in states has the guidance of those renunciates, who have embraced this secret of the universe to eliminate karmic flaws, reached us.
Guruvani
December 2003

Now, how should we take it, this is the perspective of that renouncer. How do we know that renouncer? Is it enough to see it spreading and flourishing? No. What we see is the karmic cause of its gross form. We must see how the subtle exists after completing this gross form. A karmic potential like that is a truth that remains only in the Guru of the ages. Passing this through you, you must understand an address from you in the part called father and mother. Mother, Father, Guru. Then it is said that through the knowledge in the mother, these children know what the paternal world is. Thus, having found the maternal and paternal positions, the premature deaths of that maternal lineage and the path reached thereafter. The father's too is exactly the same. After both of them have reached, that is where the part that says *Mathru Devo Bhava* must conclude. Where does it manifest and stand. Likewise, where does the deity stand. Moving from there, it is of no use saying the karma that has passed through this aeon, calling it the Guru. That is not what we need to search for, but to achieve. Achieving that should be along with the household. Otherwise, it will be like the sannyasa that comes in old age, leaving the house. That will never be right. This should not come in old age. What knowledge should a mother have before a child is born. Along with that, this father too. It is they who grow and bring this child to the Guru. So, where does the maternal nature reach, and along with it, the deities of worship that went through whichever paths of the father, do they stand in the imagination of a sage, in the imagination of a Guru, or in a simple imagination - this is an explanation. That is the vision. So, that Guru's imagination reaches everything there, and this mother, father, and Guru - these three to the disciple. That fourth imagination of God should be obtained formless. Now, where we speak of such a God and such a God, that form must be shaped by this Guru. That is the greatness of the Guru. So, this is not gross concerning you. You should not assume so. Now, among those who have come with me, there are at least six or seven people to take, to say that this is the truth. Not in the sense that they can say it exhaustively. Such truth should be taken up with our life, undertaking all the mistakes that have come into our world, and acted upon. Wearing this with determination and humility, performing karma, bringing it to virtue, that virtue must be brought to fortune. What fortune is that? The wealthy man has a fortune. There is a fortune in stating the law with this yoga. Raja Yoga is where all yogas are combined without any specific yoga. What is called Raja Yoga is not something practiced. We should not assume so. Practicing is not a Raja Yoga at all. It is a knowledge that is practiced through experience. That is what I said, what is the primordial nature of the mother and the father? What is it? Whether it is the path of the Guru, the path of the deity, or the path of the sage - the Guru shows how it has arrived and where it stands. So, in which Kali Yugas have I myself been born? How long have the Guru and disciple come and gone? Thus, how long have the god and goddess come and gone? Merely as a worm and an insect? A termite or an ant performing penance? It did that for light, but it did it, and it bore fruit. What is it? As soon as it sprouts wings and sees the light, it will run, fall there, and die. Is a light like that enough? This is what is called morphological transformation. The karma remaining in the finality of that form, remaining at the end, must be seen from there. That is a path. Then, the egg and the worm changing, thus all the eggs changing and reaching an animal-like state, how did this Guru achieve the special differences in karma that these animals exhaustively count? This is its summary. Otherwise, if you dismiss it saying that these are not things to be taken up, nothing can be taken up. This disciple must see how this Guru achieved it. It will not happen just if the Guru says it. Then, where the Guru and disciple remain, this maternal state, paternal state ڊ both having arrived, how does the Guru stand? In all of this, what does the Guru stand imagining? How does the Guru transform this into a consciousness of transition? This is the subject. Otherwise, a lot of visions come countlessly, and therefore, most people fall into the karmic flaw of counting it as bad. But do not go like that. Without going like that, we have a side. What is it? The path of the Guru.

But what should this path be? This Guru should be a disciple whom every sage and every deity worships, having attained the inner nature of this path. However long one carries such discipleship, that burden is eventually removed and shared between the Guru and the disciple. After sharing that, the next step is to unite with this Guru. Upon uniting with the Guru, the disciple must ascend yet again and stand even further ahead; they must not remain below. This is the greatness of the Guru-disciple relationship. Therefore, it requires a disciple who has grown to such a level to reveal the Guru. Otherwise, merely proclaiming it to the whole world, elaborating and attempting to perfect it, will not enable us to fulfill it. This is what I have to tell you now. You might mistakenly believe that you can ascend through various Vedantas or reach the ultimate end of the Vedas, but you will not attain it thus. That is not how it works. Growing through experiential realization in the roles of father, mother, children, and wife—in the karma of *Matru Devo Bhava* (revere the mother as God)—the extent to which we strive to sift through and resolve the past births of our mother is the duty a son or daughter must genuinely perform. It is not merely about providing rice, buttermilk, milk, and ghee; they will get those if they have money. If there is no money, they will not, and let that be. Understanding that cultivating this state is the true essence of a Guru, this Guru completely transforms the disciple into an incarnate being (*avatarapurusha*). When speaking of this incarnate being, it is not an avatar of a single era that is required. Which Manu, or how the role of the seventh Manu—Vaivasvata Manu—has been enacted and concluded, and where it presently stands, constitutes the true quest. Only by inquiring in this manner can you move forward. You must fulfill the dharma of Kali, which encompasses all good and evil, to reflect on where you stand in the karma that you understand, desire, and execute. That would be best for all of us. It is not for everyone to merely search for it; we must genuinely seek it, perfect it, and rather than just passing it to the next generation or the one after, we must integrate into the Satya Yuga along with our children and our children's children. I am telling you this with the sole desire that you become capable of a karma that helps everyone achieve this mindfully.
Guruvani
